papers.title: MusicTwins: Training Audio-Language Models to Listen like Their Persona
papers.abstract: People differ in how they perceive music, what associations they make with it, what they like about it, and how they respond to it. Computational models intended to simulate people in environments that include music should account for these differences. Although LLMs have been shown to reproduce aspects of human behavior, whether audio-language models (ALMs) can reproduce a specific person's responses to textual and musical stimuli remains underexplored. We introduce MusicTwins, a framework that combines persona summaries, personal memory, and post-training to generate person-specific responses. We construct persona representations from human writings, capturing background, views, personality, writing style, and a musical profile, and post-train Audio Flamingo Next through supervised fine-tuning and reinforcement learning. Evaluation on ten held-out personas shows notable improvements for Audio Flamingo Next in persona fidelity, including personality, writing style, and responses to music, supporting MusicTwins as a foundation for training audio-language models to listen like their persona.

papers.title: Concentrated Causal Influence, Distributed Diagnostic Information: Cognitive Impairment Decisions in Large Audio-Language Models
papers.abstract: Large audio-language models (LALMs) can assess cognitive impairment (CI) from speech, yet their answers reveal neither which internal components control the decision nor how much CI information is accessible in their representations. We investigate both questions through CI-contrast neurons (CICNs), selected by class-contrastive activation frequency in decoder MLPs. Across eight open LALMs and two corpora (Pitt and PROCESS-2), we causally test CICNs against size- and layer-matched random masks and activity-matched controls. In three of the five models that meet our eligibility criteria, ablation of small CICN sets causes large, class-directed prediction shifts; speech-identified masks also control transcript-only decisions, and three of four primary Pitt masks retain specificity on PROCESS-2. Position-restricted interventions locate the influence before the final answer position, most strongly after the speech or transcript evidence under letter-labeled options, largely as a decision-direction shift. Beyond causal localization, supervised linear readouts of frozen CICN activations achieve 0.92--0.97 AUC within Pitt, versus 0.67--0.84 for the models'direct answers. Matched random and all-neuron readouts reach comparable performance; top-ranked CICNs show only an exploratory advantage at very small unit budgets. These results distinguish concentrated causal control over output decisions from broadly distributed diagnostic information for CI detection in LALMs.

papers.title: Measuring Local Acoustic Contribution in Speech LLMs via Word-Span Counterfactual Interventions
papers.abstract: Correct transcription does not establish that a word depended on its local audio. We introduce the Acoustic Evidence Contribution (AEC), a word-level counterfactual measure of acoustic grounding. It is obtained from the change in reference-token log likelihood when the word's aligned acoustic span is replaced. We combine decoding outcomes on unedited audio with thresholded AEC in an outcome-contribution matrix, where correct targets are categorized according to their local acoustic contribution as high or low. Depending on the system, 33-49% of correct single-word targets fall below the twofold contribution threshold when averaged across corpora, despite no evident rank association with WER. Retention of reference words after span removal decreases monotonically across AEC quintiles, from 76-83% in the lowest quintile to approximately 1% in the highest. AEC therefore separates transcription correctness from dependence on the aligned local acoustic span while remaining an oracle-aligned diagnostic method.

# FineAudio-Judge

> A Fine-Grained Evaluation Framework for Complex Text-to-Audio Generation

[Code](https://github.com/QwenAudio/FunResearch/tree/main/FineAudio-Judge) |
[Benchmark](https://huggingface.co/datasets/Zixchen/FineAudio-Judge-Benchmark)

FineAudio-Judge is a fine-grained evaluation framework for assessing
whether audio matches text descriptions or generation instructions
for complex audio scenes.

Given an audio–text pair, the framework first structurally decomposes
the text into events, attributes, and inter-event relations, then
converts them into atomic binary rubric questions. The audio judge
answers each question with yes or no based on the audio, assessing
whether the audio matches the corresponding aspect of the text
description. The proportion of yes answers forms the overall
audio–text consistency score.

To train the audio judge, we construct a multi-route corpus covering
real, composed, and generated audio. Rubric-guided prompt/audio
perturbations and cross-sample mismatches provide fine-grained
supervision across varying levels of audio–text consistency.

This repository releases the resulting LoRA adapter, obtained by
supervised fine-tuning of
[Qwen3-Omni-30B-A3B-Instruct](https://huggingface.co/Qwen/Qwen3-Omni-30B-A3B-Instruct).
The adapter needs to be loaded together with the base model.
Rubric decomposition uses a separately configured language-model
backend in the
[code repository](https://github.com/QwenAudio/FunResearch/tree/main/FineAudio-Judge),
while the released adapter performs audio-based rubric judgments.

## Files

- `adapter_config.json`: PEFT LoRA configuration.
- `adapter_model.safetensors`: FineAudio-Judge LoRA adapter weights.

## Training

- **Base**: [Qwen3-Omni-30B-A3B-Instruct](https://huggingface.co/Qwen/Qwen3-Omni-30B-A3B-Instruct)
- **Corpus**: 12,508 constructed audio–prompt pairs, with 278,199 rubric-level question–answer examples used for training
- **Stage**: LoRA supervised fine-tuning with a 1-epoch training schedule
  - 8 × NVIDIA A800 80GB GPUs
  - per-device batch size 1, gradient accumulation 8
  - learning rate 5e-5
  - LoRA rank 64, alpha 64, dropout 0.05

## Usage

The evaluation scripts are provided in the
[FineAudio-Judge code repository](https://github.com/QwenAudio/FunResearch/tree/main/FineAudio-Judge).
They use ms-swift's vLLM inference engine to load
Qwen3-Omni-30B-A3B-Instruct together with the released LoRA adapter.

Clone the repository and enter the FineAudio-Judge directory:

```bash
git clone https://github.com/QwenAudio/FunResearch.git
cd FunResearch/FineAudio-Judge
```

Follow the setup instructions in the code repository's README to install
the project and configure the inference environment. Run the evaluation
commands below from the `FunResearch/FineAudio-Judge/` directory.

Replace `/path/to/benchmark` with the downloaded benchmark repository
root and `/path/to/adapter` with the directory containing the released
adapter files.

### Rubric-QA evaluation

Each audio–rubric question pair is evaluated independently.

```bash
python -m judge.cli.reproduce_rubric_qa \
  --dataset-root /path/to/benchmark \
  --model Qwen/Qwen3-Omni-30B-A3B-Instruct \
  --adapter /path/to/adapter \
  --output outputs/rubric_qa.jsonl
```

### Human-preference evaluation

Rubrics are evaluated jointly for each candidate audio, and the proportion
of yes predictions forms its prompt–audio consistency score.

```bash
python -m judge.cli.reproduce_preference \
  --dataset-root /path/to/benchmark \
  --model Qwen/Qwen3-Omni-30B-A3B-Instruct \
  --adapter /path/to/adapter \
  --output outputs/preference.jsonl
```

## License

The FineAudio-Judge LoRA adapter is released under the Apache License 2.0.
See [LICENSE](LICENSE) for details.

The adapter is fine-tuned from
[Qwen3-Omni-30B-A3B-Instruct](https://huggingface.co/Qwen/Qwen3-Omni-30B-A3B-Instruct),
which is also released under the
[Apache License 2.0](https://github.com/QwenLM/Qwen3-Omni/blob/main/LICENSE).
The base model weights are not included in this repository.

# Ultravox-Qwen3.6-27B (Base)

> [!IMPORTANT]
> **This is an early research base checkpoint** — English-only, trained on clean studio audio with **no telephony data**. If you want the model for actual voice-agent or phone-call use, get **[ultravox-qwen3.6-27b-v2](https://huggingface.co/QuantumDesk-AI/ultravox-qwen3.6-27b-v2)** — the production successor trained through Phase 1B (telephony augmentation) + Phase 2 (entity-dense + dialogue data), with published benchmarks. This checkpoint is published for reproducibility and research on the adapter-training recipe.

A speech-language model built on the Ultravox architecture, using **Qwen 3.6-27B** as the language backbone and **Whisper-large-v3-turbo** as the audio encoder. Pretrained by [Quantum Desk LTD](https://generalconcepts.ai) for real-time voice agent applications.

Unlike a cascaded ASR → LLM pipeline, this model consumes raw audio embeddings directly into the LLM's token stream — eliminating the transcription hop and cutting **200-400 ms** of latency per turn.

## Model Details

| | |
|---|---|
| Base LLM | [`Qwen/Qwen3.6-27B`](https://huggingface.co/Qwen/Qwen3.6-27B) (27B params, hybrid GDN/DeltaNet attention) |
| Audio encoder | [`openai/whisper-large-v3-turbo`](https://huggingface.co/openai/whisper-large-v3-turbo) |
| Projection adapter | Swiglu MLP, `stack_factor=8`, `hidden_size=5120` |
| Trainable params | ~100 M (projector + Whisper LoRA `r=8`) |
| Frozen params | 27 B (LLM never gradient-updated) |
| Training precision | bfloat16 |
| Recommended serve precision | Base LLM in **FP8**, projector + LoRA in bf16 |
| Language | English (base checkpoint) |
| Context length | 131 072 tokens |

## Training

- **Loss**: KL divergence to teacher (temperature 2.0)
- **Steps**: 10 000 (loss converged near step ~500, remaining steps refined the projection)
- **Effective batch**: 16 (8 × 2 gradient accumulation)
- **LR**: 5e-4 cosine → 5e-5, 500-step warmup
- **Optimizer**: AdamW
- **Hardware**: 1 × NVIDIA B200 (180 GB HBM3e), single-GPU, no FSDP
- **Wall-clock**: ~6 h 30 min
- **Whisper adaptation**: LoRA rank 8 on Whisper `k_proj`, `q_proj`, `linear_k`, `linear_q`

### Training data

English audio-transcription and audio-continuation mix (~10 datasets):

- `fixie-ai/librispeech_asr` (clean + other, continuation + transcription)
- `fixie-ai/peoplespeech-clean`
- `fixie-ai/gigaspeech-xl`
- `fixie-ai/commonvoice-en`

**This is an English-only base checkpoint.** Multilingual and phone-quality audio training were deliberately excluded to accelerate iteration and reduce cost. That broader training (Phase 1B telephony mix + Phase 2 domain data) has since shipped as **[ultravox-qwen3.6-27b-v2](https://huggingface.co/QuantumDesk-AI/ultravox-qwen3.6-27b-v2)**.

## Evaluation

Training-time metrics on `fixie-ai/librispeech-clean-transcription` (validation, 256 samples):

| Step | Eval loss |
|---|---|
| 500 | 0.442 |
| 5 000 | 0.383 |
| 9 000 | 0.381 |
| 10 000 (final) | **0.372** |

For reference, Fixie's [ultravox-v0_6-qwen-3-32b](https://huggingface.co/fixie-ai/ultravox-v0_6-qwen-3-32b) achieves **2.88 WER** on librispeech (multilingual training, 32B base).

Full WER benchmarks were measured on the successor checkpoint — **[v2 reaches 2.08% LibriSpeech test-clean WER](https://huggingface.co/QuantumDesk-AI/ultravox-qwen3.6-27b-v2#benchmarks-native-inference-greedy-n100-per-set)** — and are published on its card. This base checkpoint was not separately benchmarked.

## Usage

### With vLLM (recommended for serving)

```bash
vllm serve QuantumDesk-AI/ultravox-qwen3.6-27b-base \
  --served-model-name ultravox \
  --max-model-len 32768 \
  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.85 \
  --port 8000
```

### With transformers (for research)

```python
from transformers import AutoModel, AutoProcessor
import torchaudio

processor = AutoProcessor.from_pretrained(
    "QuantumDesk-AI/ultravox-qwen3.6-27b-base",
    trust_remote_code=True,
)
model = AutoModel.from_pretrained(
    "QuantumDesk-AI/ultravox-qwen3.6-27b-base",
    trust_remote_code=True,
    torch_dtype="bfloat16",
).to("cuda")

audio, sr = torchaudio.load("hello.wav")
messages = [
    {"role": "user", "content": [
        {"type": "audio", "audio": audio[0].numpy(), "sampling_rate": sr},
        {"type": "text", "text": "What did I say?"},
    ]},
]
inputs = processor.apply_chat_template(messages, return_tensors="pt").to("cuda")
outputs = model.generate(**inputs, max_new_tokens=128)
print(processor.decode(outputs[0], skip_special_tokens=True))
```

## Serving hardware

FP8 base + bf16 adapter fits on **any Blackwell (RTX PRO 6000, B200) or Hopper (H100 80/94GB)** GPU:

| Card | VRAM | Concurrent voice sessions* |
|---|---|---|
| RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell | 96 GB | ~30-40 |
| H100 94 GB | 94 GB | ~30-40 |
| B200 180 GB | 180 GB | ~80-100 |

*Compute-bound (KV cache is not the limit). Assumes ~2000 tokens context per session and voice-typical 5-6 tok/s per session sustained rate.

## Limitations

- **English only** — do not use for other languages; expect degraded quality even for accented English.
- **Clean audio only** — trained without phone-codec, noise, or music-background data. Real-world telephony will underperform relative to studio audio.
- **No chat / instruction tuning** — this is a base checkpoint. For interactive voice agents, fine-tune on your domain (see [Phase 2 discussion in repo]).
- **Reasoning under audio input** — some capacity is spent decoding audio; expect small (2-5 %) degradation vs pure-text prompting on reasoning-heavy tasks. Use text cascade for complex queries.

## License

Apache 2.0. Model weights are Quantum Desk LTD's contribution. See individual base-model licenses for [Qwen 3.6-27B](https://huggingface.co/Qwen/Qwen3.6-27B) (Apache 2.0) and [Whisper-large-v3-turbo](https://huggingface.co/openai/whisper-large-v3-turbo) (MIT).

- [Qwen team](https://huggingface.co/Qwen) — 3.6-27B base
- [OpenAI](https://huggingface.co/openai/whisper-large-v3-turbo) — Whisper encoder

Audio8 TTS Preview 0.1B

**The smallest zero-shot TTS worth running.** [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Audio8__TTS-black?style=for-the-badge&logo=github)](https://github.com/Audio8-AI/Audio8_TTS) [![Demo-0.1B Audio Samples](https://img.shields.io/badge/Demo--0.1B-Audio%20Samples-brightgreen?style=for-the-badge&logo=githubpages)](https://edge0-ai.github.io/Audio8_TTS/0.1B/)

🎬Teaser video

**Audio8 TTS 0.1B** supports speech generation and zero-shot voice cloning. This repository contains the complete v4 mixed checkpoint, its neural audio codec, tokenizer, processor, and Hugging Face remote code. ## Compact Scale The defining characteristic of this release is its size. The main generative model is approximately **170M parameters**, while the codec decoder is a separate approximately **120M-parameter** component. Even counting the codec decoder, the complete audio generation stack remains much smaller than most modern multilingual TTS systems. | Model | Reported main-model scale | |---|---:| | **Audio8 TTS Preview 0.1B** | **~0.17B** | | Audio8 TTS Preview 0.6B | ~0.6B | | IndexTTS2.5 | ~0.8B | | CosyVoice3 | ~1.5B | | VoxCPM2 | ~2.3B | | Fish S2 Pro | ~4.6B | | Higgs Audio v2 | ~4.7B | | MOSS-TTS | ~8.5B | These figures are approximate reference scales collected from the respective model reports and are not a strictly matched parameter-count audit. The 0.1B checkpoint is intended to make zero-shot TTS practical with a much smaller language/audio model footprint, not to claim identical quality across every language or benchmark. ## Supported Languages - Primary: Chinese and English - Experimental/multilingual evaluation: German, Spanish, French, Italian, Japanese, and Korean ## Model Details The model uses an Audio8 Falcon H1 architecture with slow and fast autoregressive branches. The slow branch predicts semantic tokens, while the fast branch predicts codec codebooks conditioned on the slow hidden state. | Component | Configuration | |---|---| | Main model | Approximately 170M parameters, excluding the codec decoder | | Slow AR | 24 layers, width 512, 8 attention heads, 2 KV heads | | Fast AR | 4 layers, width 512, 8 attention heads, 2 KV heads | | Acoustic tokens | 10 codebooks, 4,096 entries per codebook | | Codec | 44.1 kHz, 2,048 samples per model frame (~21.5 frames/s) | | Codec decoder | Approximately 120M parameters; bundled in `codec.pth` | | Context | Up to 2,048 packed text/audio positions | The codec is included in this repository. No additional codec checkpoint is required. ## Deployment Options ### CPU deployment: ONNX INT8 [Audio8-TTS-Preview-0.1B-ONNX-INT8](https://huggingface.co/Audio8/audio8-TTS-0.1B-ONNX-INT8) packages Audio8 TTS for low-resource CPU inference with ONNX Runtime. Slow and Fast AR use per-token INT8 graphs, while the neural audio codec uses FP16. | Advantage | Details | | ----------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------ | | CPU native | Runs with ONNX Runtime `CPUExecutionProvider`; no CUDA required | | Low memory | About **0.4 GiB after loading** in the tested Linux x86_64 configuration | | Small runtime | No PyTorch or Transformers dependency after model download | | Complete workflow | CLI, web and HTTP service, streaming PCM, and voice registration | Normal synthesis loads only the Slow AR, Fast AR, and codec decoder sessions. Voice registration releases those sessions before loading the optional codec encoder, keeping peak memory controlled. Get the [ONNX INT8 model](https://huggingface.co/Audio8/audio8-TTS-0.1B-ONNX-INT8) and follow the [CPU ONNX Runtime guide](https://github.com/Audio8-AI/Audio8_TTS/tree/master/onnx_runtime). ## Installation Python 3.11 or newer and a CUDA-capable GPU are recommended. ```bash pip install "torch>=2.5.0" "torchaudio>=2.5.0" \ "transformers>=4.57.0,<5" "soundfile>=0.12" "safetensors>=0.4" ``` ## Usage The model includes custom Transformers code. Load it with `trust_remote_code=True`. ### Voice cloning The primary usage of this checkpoint is zero-shot voice cloning. Replace `reference.wav` and the reference transcript with your own audio and text. The reference transcript should match the spoken content of the reference audio. ```python import soundfile as sf import torch from transformers import AutoModel, AutoProcessor model_id = "Audio8/Audio8-TTS-Preview-0.1b" device = "cuda" if torch.cuda.is_available() else "cpu" dtype = torch.bfloat16 if device == "cuda" else torch.float32 processor = AutoProcessor.from_pretrained( model_id, trust_remote_code=True, ) model = AutoModel.from_pretrained( model_id, trust_remote_code=True, dtype=dtype, ).eval().to(device) inputs = processor( text=["这是一个语音合成测试。"], reference_audio=["reference.wav"], reference_text=["参考音频对应的完整文本。"], return_tensors="pt", ) inputs = {name: value.to(device) for name, value in inputs.items()} with torch.inference_mode(): output = model.generate( **inputs, max_new_tokens=512, temperature=0.7, top_p=0.9, top_k=50, do_sample=True, return_dict_in_generate=True, ) waveforms, waveform_lengths = model.decode_audio(output.codes) audio = waveforms[0, : int(waveform_lengths[0])].float().cpu().numpy() sf.write("output.wav", audio, model.config.codec_sample_rate) ``` For synthesis without cloning, omit `reference_audio` and `reference_text`. For batch inference with audio or pre-encoded reference codes, see the Audio8 TTS training and inference repository. ## Evaluation Lower WER/CER is better; higher SIM (similarity) is better. ### CV3 error-rate comparison Lower is better. These comparison values follow the evaluation table published for Audio8 TTS Preview 0.6B; they are reference comparisons rather than a strictly matched re-evaluation. | Model | Parameters | zh | en | ja | ko | de | es | fr | it | |---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:| | **Audio8 TTS Preview 0.1B** | **~0.17B** | 3.619 | 3.307 | 12.322 | 7.653 | 5.292 | 8.548 | 12.349 | 14.480 | | Audio8 TTS Preview 0.6B | 0.6B | **3.205** | **3.128** | 7.205 | 4.223 | 3.447 | 3.641 | 8.790 | 4.790 | | Fish S2 Pro | 4.6B | 3.600 | 3.493 | 5.139 | **4.111** | 3.605 | 2.972 | **8.600** | 4.229 | | Higgs Audio v2 | 4.7B | 3.378 | 3.404 | **4.742** | 4.260 | **3.300** | **2.929** | 9.425 | **3.555** | | CosyVoice3-1.5B | 1.5B | 3.91 | 4.99 | 7.57 | 5.69 | 6.43 | 4.47 | 11.8 | 10.5 | | VoxCPM2 | 2.3B | 3.65 | 5.00 | 5.96 | 5.69 | 4.77 | 3.80 | 9.85 | 4.25 | | IndexTTS2.5 | 0.8B | 4.36 | 5.12 | 5.66 | - | - | 3.75 | - | - | ### Seed-TTS comparison Similarity values are shown as percentages in this comparison table. Lower WER/CER is better; higher similarity is better. | Model | Parameters | EN WER / SIM | ZH CER / SIM | |---|---:|---:|---:| | **Audio8 TTS Preview 0.1B** | **~0.17B** | 1.662 / 56.7 | 1.13 / 68.2 | | Audio8 TTS Preview 0.6B | 0.6B | **1.506** / 63.2 | 0.950 / 73.1 | | Fish S2 Pro | 4.6B | 1.607 / 64.6 | 1.038 / 73.8 | | Higgs Audio v2 | 4.7B | 1.524 / 66.4 | **0.806** / 72.1 | | CosyVoice3-1.5B | 1.5B | 2.22 / 72.0 | 1.12 / 78.1 | | MOSS-TTS | 8.5B | 1.85 / 73.4 | 1.20 / 78.8 | | VoxCPM2 | 2.3B | 1.84 / 75.3 | 0.97 / 79.5 | | IndexTTS2.5 | 0.8B | 3.253 / **82.3** | 1.119 / **80.4** | The IndexTTS2.5 row uses the Token-Level Concatenation result from the Seed-TTS-Eval portion of Table 1 in the IndexTTS 2.5 technical report. Parameter scales are approximate reference values from the respective model reports (see the Compact Scale section); they are not a strictly matched parameter-count audit. For reference, MOSS-TTS contains 8,489,841,664 parameters and VoxCPM2's main model contains 2,290,004,544 parameters; the separate AudioVAE is not included in the parameter comparison. Fish S2 Pro was reevaluated because its official evaluation uses its own normalizer. Higgs Audio v2 was evaluated locally because concrete values were unavailable. All other baseline values were collected from their official reports through the [VoxCPM repository](https://github.com/OpenBMB/VoxCPM). Different normalizers and evaluators make cross-project values reference comparisons rather than a strictly matched ranking. Evaluation coverage does not expand the Preview checkpoint's supported-language claim beyond the languages listed above. ## Limitations and Responsible Use - This is a compact preview checkpoint. # Maya 2 Native **Open speech. Native voices.** Streaming text-to-speech for **11 Indic languages and English**. **12 languages · 20 voices · Voice cloning · Apache-2.0** [Listen](#listen-in-12-languages) · [Get started](#quickstart) · [Explore voices](#voices) · [Benchmarks](#voicearena-benchmark) · [Evaluation](#evaluation) · [Code](https://github.com/MayaResearch/maya2-native)
Maya 2 Native brings streaming speech generation to the languages people use every day. Built by **Maya Research**, it generates **24 kHz speech** in 12 languages, with **20 built-in voices** and **zero-shot voice cloning from 3–10 seconds of reference audio**. A voice can speak across languages: a Hindi reference can become Tamil speech. Use it to give a voice agent its next turn, read a story in a familiar language, or build a multilingual interface you can host yourself. The release includes **open weights and inference code**, with a Python API, an OpenAI-compatible speech endpoint, and WebSocket streaming. Assamese is cross-lingual for every built-in voice; see [limitations](#limitations). ## Quickstart Use **Linux, Python 3.10–3.12, and an NVIDIA GPU with a driver supporting CUDA 12.8**. Start with `max_seats=1`. The documented single-seat loading peak is approximately 9.2 GB plus CUDA context; a 12 GB or larger GPU provides more room. See [hardware and memory](#hardware-and-memory) before increasing concurrency. ```bash python -m venv .venv source .venv/bin/activate pip install "maya3[server] @ git+https://github.com/MayaResearch/maya2-native" \ --extra-index-url https://download.pytorch.org/whl/cu128 ``` ### Generate speech ```python import soundfile as sf from maya3 import Maya3TTS tts = Maya3TTS.from_pretrained("maya-research/maya2-native", max_seats=1) audio = tts.generate( "नमस्ते, आपका ऑर्डर कल पहुँच जाएगा।", lang="hi", voice="Ahana", normalize=True, ) sf.write("speech.wav", audio, 24000) tts.close() ``` `generate()` returns a mono NumPy waveform in `float32`. Model weights, the Mimi codec, and the ECAPA speaker encoder are downloaded on first use. For offline inference, cache all three first, then set `HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1`. **Normalization differs by interface:** the HTTP and WebSocket servers enable it by default. The Python API requires `normalize=True`. It expands numbers, currency, dates, times, URLs, email addresses, and other written forms into spoken text. Check the output for unusual formats.
Stream audio as it is generated ### Stream speech ```python from maya3 import Maya3TTS tts = Maya3TTS.from_pretrained("maya-research/maya2-native", max_seats=1) try: with open("speech.pcm", "wb") as output: for chunk in tts.stream( "Your order has shipped and will arrive tomorrow.", lang="en", voice="Siddhant", normalize=True, ): output.write(chunk.astype(" ### Clone a voice across languages Use a clean, single-speaker reference clip and its exact transcript. Obtain the speaker's permission before cloning their voice. The reference language and the output language can differ. ```python import soundfile as sf from maya3 import Maya3TTS tts = Maya3TTS.from_pretrained("maya-research/maya2-native", max_seats=1) tts.register_voice( "my_voice", ref_audio="reference.wav", # 3–10 seconds recommended ref_text="", lang="hi", # reference language ) audio = tts.generate( "வணக்கம், எப்படி இருக்கிறீர்கள்?", lang="ta", # output language voice="my_voice", normalize=True, ) sf.write("cloned_voice_tamil.wav", audio, 24000) tts.close() ``` The default cloning mode, `icl_spk`, combines the reference audio with an ECAPA speaker embedding. Clones approximate the reference voice; similarity and accent vary. A dedicated cloning benchmark is not included in this release's reported results.
Run a local HTTP and WebSocket server ### Serve over HTTP or WebSocket ```bash python -m maya3.server \ --ckpt maya-research/maya2-native \ --host 127.0.0.1 --port 8080 --max-seats 1 ``` After `GET /health` reports ready, generate speech: ```bash curl --fail-with-body -sS http://127.0.0.1:8080/v1/audio/speech \ -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \ -d '{"input":"Your order has shipped.","language":"en","voice":"Ahana","response_format":"wav"}' \ --output speech.wav ``` The server provides `POST /v1/audio/speech`, `WS /v1/tts/stream`, and voice registration endpoints. It has no built-in authentication; add authentication and access controls before exposing it beyond a trusted environment. See the [GitHub README](https://github.com/MayaResearch/maya2-native#serve-the-model) for clients and protocol details.

Three ASR judges measured intelligibility; a speaker-embedding classifier measured consistency among the 20 built-in voices. **These are Maya Research's release measurements.** ASR error rates and embedding similarity capture specific aspects of quality; they do not replace human listening or measure every aspect of naturalness. Serving measurements below describe the tested hardware and workload. ### Benchmark design The release benchmark, **bench6k**, contains **6,000 held-out texts: 500 per language across 31 content categories**, including conversation, names, numbers, dates, currency, addresses, URLs, code-mixed text, tongue twisters, and prompts of 1–50 words. The release documentation states that these evaluation texts were excluded from training. The benchmark produced **20.3 hours of speech** through the server, with normalization and engine guards enabled, sampled decoding, and one seed per row. Voices were distributed across languages and categories; long inputs used the serving stack's text chunking. Three ASR systems transcribed the generated speech: - **ASR-1:** Maya's in-house Indic ASR and primary judge. - **Qwen3-ASR:** a third ASR judge. - **ASR-2:** a second in-house Indic ASR, held out from training, reward generation, and checkpoint selection. **Character error rate (CER)** compares ASR transcripts with spoken-form references. Scorer v1 uses the benchmark's normalization and script harmonization. Scorer v2 additionally harmonizes Latin and native-script spellings in code-mixed spans. The two scorers evaluate the same generated audio; lower v2 scores reflect a scoring change. | Overall CER ↓ | ASR-1 | Qwen3-ASR | ASR-2, held out | |---|---:|---:|---:| | Scorer v1 | 3.49% | 3.40% | 2.86% | | Scorer v2, additional code-mix harmonization | 2.35% | 2.22% | 1.73% | ### Results by language CER below uses **scorer v1**. Architecture and audio generation ## Architecture Maya 2 Native generates discrete audio tokens autoregressively, then decodes them into speech with Mimi. | Component | Description | |---|---| | Text and audio backbone | Initialized from [Qwen3-1.7B-Base](https://huggingface.co/Qwen/Qwen3-1.7B-Base); 28 layers, hidden size 2,048, 16 attention heads and 8 KV heads; extended vocabulary for language and audio tokens | | Depth decoder | Approximately 555M parameters; predicts codebooks 1–31 after the backbone predicts codebook 0 | | Audio codec | [Kyutai Mimi](https://huggingface.co/kyutai/mimi); 32 codebooks with 2,048 entries each, at 12.5 frames per second | | Speaker conditioning | 192-dimensional [SpeechBrain ECAPA-TDNN](https://huggingface.co/speechbrain/spkrec-ecapa-voxceleb) embedding projected into the backbone; reference-audio conditioning for cloning | | Output | 24 kHz mono speech, 80 ms per audio frame | At each step, the backbone predicts the first codebook, the depth decoder fills the remaining codebooks, and Mimi decodes an audio frame. The engine can emit that frame while generation continues. An end-of-audio token controls normal stopping; duration and loop guards provide additional controls.
## Training data and procedure The release documentation describes a mixture of **licensed and synthetic speech with transcripts** across the 12 languages, plus text-only data used to adapt the backbone to the languages. The built-in voice personas use synthetic and licensed voice data prepared for this purpose. The preference-optimization stage used **direct preference optimization (DPO)** on model-generated candidates ranked by ASR agreement and speaker similarity. Benchmark texts were excluded from training, according to the release documentation. Dataset identities, total training hours, detailed per-language composition, and the full training configuration are not disclosed in this release. Automated scores should be considered alongside these disclosure limits. ## Limitations - **Uneven language coverage.** Assamese is the most challenging Indic language in the release benchmark. No built-in voice has at least one hour of Assamese training data; some outputs drift toward a Bengali-like timbre. Other cross-lingual combinations can also carry the voice's training-language accent. - **Very short turns.** One- or two-word prompts are less stable in voice identity, and speaker-embedding evaluation is less reliable on very short clips. A slightly longer phrase may help short agent responses. - **Code-mixed and written-form inputs.** English words inside Indic sentences vary by voice. URLs, symbols, dates, and long digit sequences remain difficult, even with normalization. Listen to application-specific examples before relying on them. - **Voice cloning.** Similarity is approximate. Noise, multiple speakers, short references, and inaccurate transcripts can degrade results. Dedicated zero-shot cloning scores are not reported here. - **Emotion and events.** Tags such as `[laughs]`, `[sighs]`, `[whispers]`, `[sad]`, and `[excited]` are best effort and were not the focus of this release. - **Generation and guards.** Sampling can produce errors. The same seed is reproducible for an isolated request, but batching changes the random stream. Loop and duration guards can end genuinely repetitive text early. No benchmark clip spoke a built-in voice name aloud, but this remains a possible failure mode. - **Evaluation scope.** Results use automated ASR and speaker-embedding judges. This card does not report a human naturalness study, comprehensive dialect or demographic evaluation, confidence intervals, or a controlled comparison with other TTS models. ## Intended use and responsible deployment Maya 2 Native is intended for voice interfaces and agents, accessibility, reading and narration, IVR, notifications, and research on multilingual speech generation. Clone only voices you own or have explicit permission to use. Disclose synthetic speech to listeners, especially in calls and media. Do not use the model for deceptive impersonation, fraud, harassment, non-consensual content, disinformation, or attempts to defeat voice authentication. Built-in voice names identify synthetic personas and should not be presented as real people. **This release does not add an audio watermark.** Applications should implement the consent, disclosure, access controls, and abuse monitoring appropriate to their use. Consult the repository's [security guidance](https://github.com/MayaResearch/maya2-native/blob/main/SECURITY.md) for deployment considerations.

7.9B-A1.3B multilingual MoE speech synthesis with paralinguistic and free-form control.

GitHub | Blog & Demos | ModelScope

This repository contains **Ming-3.0-tts-tiny**, the Ming-3.0-tts mixture-of-experts checkpoint built on Ling V3. Its Ling V3 backbone has 7.9B total parameters and activates about 1.3B parameters per token. The repository includes sharded weights, supporting model code, audio tokenizer, speaker encoder and text tokenizer. > **Inference requires the [Ming-3.0-tts GitHub repository](https://github.com/inclusionAI/Ming-3.0-tts).** This Hugging Face repository is for checkpoint distribution and does not provide a standalone inference setup. Clone the GitHub repository and follow its README for the current dependencies, inference code and usage instructions. The CLI scripts and Python APIs referenced below are provided by the GitHub repository. ## Model Details | Item | Value | | --- | --- | | Architecture | Mixture of Experts, Ling V3 backbone | | Backbone parameters | 7.9B total, about 1.3B active per token | | Languages | Chinese, English, German, Spanish, French, Korean, Japanese | | Dialects | Sichuanese, Cantonese | | Python API | `ming_tiny.MingTinyTTS` | | CLI | `infer_tiny.py` | | Prompt protocol | `thinking_v1` | ## Capabilities - Zero-shot voice cloning from a short reference clip - Voice Design from a natural-language speaker description - Free-form control of delivery and speaking style - Built-in Chinese and English voices - Multilingual synthesis and Sichuanese/Cantonese dialect control - 14 inline tags for breath, cough, sigh, laughter, hesitation, surprise and question/confirmation sounds in Chinese or English - Explicit emotion, speed, pitch and volume control - Multi-speaker dialogue from a script and speaker references (`podcast`) Recommended built-in voices: **UK_George**, **US_Emma**, **灵小柔** and **灵楷**. See the [voice catalog](https://github.com/inclusionAI/Ming-3.0-tts/blob/main/cookbooks/instruction_en.md#built-in-premium-voices) for the full list and voice descriptions. ## Quick Start ### Installation ```bash git clone https://github.com/inclusionAI/Ming-3.0-tts.git cd Ming-3.0-tts conda create -n ming-tiny python=3.10.15 -y conda activate ming-tiny pip install -r requirements-tiny.txt ``` Tiny uses a separate reference inference environment: Python **3.10.15**, PyTorch and torchaudio **2.7.1+cu118** (CUDA 11.8 wheels), and `transformers==4.46.3`. Install the pinned dependencies from [requirements-tiny.txt](https://github.com/inclusionAI/Ming-3.0-tts/blob/main/requirements-tiny.txt) in a dedicated environment, as other dependency versions differ from 0.5B. We recommend using NVIDIA H800 for inference. ### Download ```bash pip install "huggingface_hub[cli]" hf download inclusionAI/Ming-3.0-tts-tiny --local-dir Ming-3.0-tts-tiny ``` ### CLI Inference ```bash python infer_tiny.py \ --model_path inclusionAI/Ming-3.0-tts-tiny \ --task dialect \ --text "今日天气几好，我哋食完饭一齐去海边行下啦。" \ --dialect 广粤话 \ --prompt_wav data/wavs/10002287-00000094.wav \ --output_path output/tiny.wav ``` ### Python API Loading configures the release runtime (bf16, portable MoE loop, fp32 recurrent state) and checks the checkpoint against it; `generate()` defaults to `cfg_scale=2.0`, `temperature=0`, `flow_steps=10`, and `sigma=0.25`. ```python from ming_tiny import MingTinyTTS tts = MingTinyTTS.from_pretrained("inclusionAI/Ming-3.0-tts-tiny", device="cuda:0") tts.generate( task="seed", text="傍晚的风从山口吹过来，远处的云慢慢染成了金色。", prompt_wav="data/wavs/10002287-00000094.wav", prompt_text="在此奉劝大家别乱打美白针。", target_language="Chinese", # English for English text output_path="outputs/seed.wav", ) ``` ### Supported Tasks Each call selects one task and accepts the inputs listed below: | Task | Reference audio | Reference text | `target_language` | Controls | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | `seed` | one | required | `Chinese` / `English`, required | — | | `multilingual` | one | required | `German` / `Spanish` / `French` / `Korean` / `Japanese` | — | | `paralinguistic` | one | required | `Chinese` / `English` | inline tags in `text` | | `podcast` | one per speaker | one per speaker, same order | inferred from the text | `speaker_N:` at the start of every line | | `basic` | one | not accepted | — | `speed`, `pitch`, `volume`, all three | | `emotion` | one | not accepted | — | `emotion` | | `dialect` | one | not accepted | — | `dialect`: `川渝话` / `广粤话` | | `freeform` | one | not accepted | — | `instruction` | | `voice_design` | none | — | — | `style` | | `ip` | none | — | — | `ip` | Freeform always requires a reference clip and cannot be combined with voice design, a built-in voice, emotion, dialect or attribute controls. For `podcast`, start every dialogue line with `speaker_N:` and provide one reference audio clip and transcript per speaker, in speaker order. Repeat `--prompt_wav` and `--prompt_text` on the command line. See the [Tiny examples](https://github.com/inclusionAI/Ming-3.0-tts#ming-30-tts-tiny) for a Podcast Python example and [examples/one_click/](https://github.com/inclusionAI/Ming-3.0-tts/tree/main/examples/one_click) for scripts for every task. `python infer_tiny.py --help` lists the CLI arguments. ### Verify the Checkpoint ```bash python tools/preflight_tiny.py --model_path /path/to/Ming-3.0-tts-tiny ``` ## Serving with vLLM-Omni For installation, follow the [vLLM-Omni official installation guide](https://docs.vllm.ai/projects/vllm-omni/en/latest/getting_started/installation/); [vLLM-Omni](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-omni) serves this checkpoint through the OpenAI-compatible `/v1/audio/speech` endpoint. The current recipe targets vLLM 0.32.0. Use a separate environment from the reference inference setup above. Start the server in one terminal: ```bash vllm serve inclusionAI/Ming-3.0-tts-tiny --omni --port 8000 ``` The HF model ID selects the two-stage Ming3-TTS pipeline automatically and downloads the weights and required assets on first launch. Both stages share GPU 0. A complete local model directory may also be used; pass `--revision ` to pin a remote checkpoint. After the server is ready, run this reference-free voice design example in another terminal: ```bash curl --fail-with-body --silent --show-error http://127.0.0.1:8000/v1/audio/speech \ -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \ -d '{ "model": "inclusionAI/Ming-3.0-tts-tiny", "input": "傍晚的风从山口吹过来，远处的云慢慢染成了金色。", "instructions": "{\"风格\":\"年轻女声，声音清晰自然。\"}", "response_format": "wav", "extra_params": {"temperature": 0.0, "ming3_cfg": 1.0}, "seed": 1234 }' --output ming3_tiny_design.wav ``` The output is a mono 44.1 kHz WAV. Voice cloning uses `ref_audio` and its matching transcript in `ref_text`; speech controls use `instructions`. For voice cloning, dialect and emotion controls, built-in voices, multi-speaker Podcast, and PCM streaming, see the upstream [Ming-3.0-TTS recipe](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-omni/blob/main/recipes/inclusionAI/Ming-3.0-TTS.md). ## Serving with SGLang-Omni [SGLang-Omni](https://sgl-project.github.io/sglang-omni/) serves this checkpoint on one GPU: ```bash sgl-omni serve --model-path inclusionAI/Ming-3.0-tts-tiny ``` Synthesize speech through the OpenAI-compatible endpoint: ```bash curl -X POST http://127.0.0.1:8000/v1/audio/speech \ -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -d '{ "model": "inclusionAI/Ming-3.0-tts-tiny", "input": "Get the trust fund to the bank early.", "response_format": "wav", "seed": 123 }' \ --output speech.wav ``` `response_format` accepts `wav`, `mp3`, `flac`, and `pcm`. [![GitHub](./assets/badges/github-badge.svg)](https://github.com/Edge0-AI/Audio8_TTS) [![License](./assets/badges/license-badge.svg)](./LICENSE) [![Demo](./assets/badges/demo-badge.svg)](https://edge0-ai.github.io/Audio8_TTS/realistic-0.6b/) [![arXiv](./assets/badges/arxiv-badge.svg)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.14776) [![Playground](./assets/badges/playground-badge.svg)](https://huggingface.co/spaces/Edge0/Audio8-TTS-Realistic-0.6b) [Languages](#supported-languages) · [Quick start](#installation) · [Serving](#high-throughput-serving-sglang-omni) · [Evaluation](#evaluation)
--- **Audio8-TTS-Realistic-0.6B** builds on [Audio8-TTS-Preview-0.6b](https://huggingface.co/Edge0/Audio8-TTS-Preview-0.6b), delivering **substantially improved speech realism** while retaining its compact **0.6B** architecture and zero-shot voice cloning capabilities. This release supports **23 languages**, adding **12 languages compared with Preview**. It uses the same Transformers inference interface as Preview. This repository includes the complete model checkpoint, its 44.1 kHz neural audio codec, tokenizer, processor, and custom Transformers code. Try speech generation and voice cloning in the [interactive Playground](https://huggingface.co/spaces/Edge0/Audio8-TTS-Realistic-0.6b). Hosted on Hugging Face ZeroGPU; availability depends on the queue and your daily GPU allowance. Audio8 is also participating in [TTS Arena](https://tts-agi-tts-arena-v2.hf.space/), where it has received encouraging ratings from listeners. We are grateful to everyone who has listened and voted. ## Highlights - **Improved realism:** more natural prosody and expressive delivery, building on Preview. - **Broader multilingual coverage:** 23 languages, including 12 additions to Preview's 11 supported languages. - **Compact model:** 601 million main-model parameters, with the audio codec bundled separately. - **Flexible generation:** zero-shot voice cloning from a reference recording and transcript, or speech generation without a reference. - **GPU serving:** an SGLang Omni adapter with paged attention, dynamic batching, and an OpenAI-compatible speech API. ## Supported Languages | Coverage | Languages | |---|---| | Supported in Preview (11) | Cantonese, Chinese, Dutch, English, French, German, Italian, Japanese, Korean, Polish, Spanish | | Added in Realistic (12) | Arabic, Finnish, Hindi, Indonesian, Malay, Norwegian, Portuguese, Russian, Swedish, Thai, Turkish, Vietnamese | > **Note:** Language quality varies; see the per-language evaluation below. Benchmark coverage includes some additional languages and is distinct from the supported-language list. ## Model Details Audio8 TTS uses a DualAR architecture inspired by [Fish Audio S2 Pro](https://github.com/fishaudio/fish-speech). The slow AR transformer predicts one semantic token for each audio frame. The fast AR transformer predicts the frame's codec codebooks, conditioned on the slow hidden state and preceding codebooks. | Component | Configuration | |---|---| | Main model | 601,159,424 parameters, excluding the codec | | Slow AR | 24 layers, width 896, 14 attention heads, 2 KV heads | | Fast AR | 4 layers, width 896, 14 attention heads, 2 KV heads | | Acoustic tokens | 10 codebooks, 4,096 entries per codebook | | Codec | 44.1 kHz, 2,048 samples per model frame (~21.5 frames/s) | | Context | Up to 2,048 packed text/audio positions | The bundled codec handles both reference-audio encoding and waveform decoding, so no additional codec checkpoint is required. The **0.6B** size refers to the main DualAR model; the codec is excluded from that parameter count. --- ## Installation Python 3.10 or newer and a CUDA-capable GPU are recommended. ```bash pip install "torch>=2.5.0" "torchaudio>=2.5.0" \ "transformers>=4.57.0,<5" "soundfile>=0.12" "safetensors>=0.4" ``` The Transformers release package was smoke-tested with PyTorch 2.8.0 and Transformers 4.57.3 on an NVIDIA H20 using BF16. Checks covered model loading, English and Chinese generation with and without reference audio, and generation in Arabic, Cantonese, Portuguese, and Russian. These are runtime checks, separate from the benchmark results below. ## Usage The model uses custom Transformers code. Review the files in this repository, then load it with `trust_remote_code=True`. ### Zero-shot voice cloning Use a clean reference recording. Its transcript must match the spoken content exactly. ```python import soundfile as sf import torch from transformers import AutoModel, AutoProcessor model_id = "Edge0/Audio8-TTS-Realistic-0.6b" device = "cuda" if torch.cuda.is_available() else "cpu" dtype = torch.bfloat16 if device == "cuda" else torch.float32 processor = AutoProcessor.from_pretrained(model_id, trust_remote_code=True) model = AutoModel.from_pretrained( model_id, trust_remote_code=True, dtype=dtype, ).eval().to(device) inputs = processor( text=["Welcome to Audio8 TTS. It is wonderful to hear from you."], reference_audio=["reference.wav"], reference_text=["The exact transcript of the reference recording."], return_tensors="pt", ) inputs = {name: value.to(device) for name, value in inputs.items()} with torch.inference_mode(): output = model.generate( **inputs, max_new_tokens=1024, temperature=0.8, top_p=0.95, top_k=50, do_sample=True, return_dict_in_generate=True, ) waveforms, waveform_lengths = model.decode_audio(output.codes) audio = waveforms[0, : int(waveform_lengths[0])].float().cpu().numpy() sf.write("output.wav", audio, model.config.codec_sample_rate) ``` ### Generation without a reference Replace the processor call above with: ```python inputs = processor( text=["This utterance does not use a reference voice."], return_tensors="pt", ) ``` Then move the inputs to the model device and run the same generation and decoding steps. For command-line inference, batching, and supervised fine-tuning, see the [Audio8 TTS repository](https://github.com/Edge0-AI/Audio8_TTS), using `Edge0/Audio8-TTS-Realistic-0.6b` as the model path. ## High-throughput serving: SGLang Omni The [SGLang Omni adapter](https://github.com/Edge0-AI/Audio8_TTS/tree/master/sglang_omni) provides GPU serving for Audio8 TTS. It is installed as an independent model plugin and does not overwrite SGLang Omni core files. | Capability | Support | |---|---| | Attention and batching | SGLang paged attention and dynamic batching | | DualAR execution | Slow AR serving with a fixed KV cache for the Fast AR codebook decoder | | Voice cloning | Reference-audio encoding and waveform decoding | | API | OpenAI-compatible `/v1/audio/speech` service | Use the **0.6B** configuration, `sglang_omni/configs/audio8_tts_0_6b.yaml`, and set the model path to `Edge0/Audio8-TTS-Realistic-0.6b` or its downloaded snapshot. The adapter supports generation without a reference and zero-shot voice cloning. See the [deployment guide](https://github.com/Edge0-AI/Audio8_TTS#sglang-omni-serving) for compatible dependency versions, installation, server configuration, and API examples. > **Validation note:** Audio8-TTS-Realistic was tested on an NVIDIA H20 in BF16 for generation with and without a reference through the non-streaming speech API, with Torch compilation and CUDA graphs disabled. These checks validate runtime compatibility; throughput and streaming were not benchmarked. --- ## Evaluation Error rates are percentages (**lower is better**). Speaker similarity (SIM) is on a **0–1 scale** (**higher is better**). These metrics measure intelligibility and speaker similarity; they do not directly measure perceived speech realism. ### Benchmark summary **Audio8-TTS-Preview** and **Audio8-TTS-Realistic**, both **0.6B**: | Benchmark | Coverage | Preview error % ↓ | Realistic error % ↓ | Preview SIM ↑ | Realistic SIM ↑ | |---|---|---:|---:|---:|---:| | Seed-TTS | English / Chinese | 1.23 | 1.25 | 0.682 | 0.704 | | CV3 | 8 shared languages | 4.80 | 4.56 | — | 0.663 | | CV3 | 9 core languages | — | 4.86 | — | 0.661 | | MiniMax | 24 evaluated languages | — | 5.89 | — | 0.754 | > **Note:** Values are unweighted language macro averages. Preview results are calculated from its [published model card](https://huggingface.co/Edge0/Audio8-TTS-Preview-0.6b#evaluation), with SIM converted from percentages to a 0–1 scale. The two releases were evaluated separately. A dash means the corresponding result was not reported on Preview's card. > > Seed-TTS averages English WER and Chinese CER, excluding hard Chinese. The shared CV3 subset is Chinese, English, Japanese, Korean, German, French, Spanish, and Italian; the 9-language set also includes Russian. CV3 averages exclude hard subsets and the 13 additional languages. MiniMax averages all 24 evaluated languages, including languages outside the supported list. ### Reference comparison The following error rates come from the sources used in our technical report. Different evaluation pipelines and text normalization make this a reference comparison rather than a strictly matched ranking. A dash means that a result is unavailable in the comparison, not that the model lacks support. | Model | Parameters (B) | Seed-TTS EN/ZH error ↓ | CV3 (9) error ↓ | MiniMax (24) error ↓ | |---|---:|---:|---:|---:| | **Audio8-TTS-Realistic** | **0.6** | **1.25** | **4.86** | **5.89** | | Qwen3-TTS-12Hz-0.6B | 0.6 | 1.12 | — | — | | Qwen3-TTS-1.7B | 1.7 | 1.01 | 7.73 | 27.41 | | Higgs Audio v3 | 4 | 1.11 | 4.41 | 2.74 | | Higgs Audio v2 | 4.7 | 1.17 | 4.49 | — | | Fish S2 Pro | 4.6 | 1.32 | 4.49 | 4.40 | | MOSS-TTS-v1.5 | 8.5 | 1.52 | 6.11 | 3.78 | | CosyVoice3-1.5B | 1.5 | 1.67 | 6.89 | — | | VoxCPM2 | 2.3 | 1.41 | 5.35 | — | > **Sources:** Qwen Seed-TTS results are from the Qwen3-TTS report, linked from the [official Qwen3-TTS repository](https://github.com/QwenLM/Qwen3-TTS); Qwen's CV3/MiniMax results, all Higgs Audio v3 results, and MOSS-TTS-v1.5's CV3/MiniMax results are from [Boson AI's evaluation](https://huggingface.co/bosonai/higgs-audio-v3-tts-4b). Fish S2 Pro's MiniMax result is from the Fish Audio S2 report, linked from the [official Fish Speech repository](https://github.com/fishaudio/fish-speech); its Seed-TTS/CV3 results and Higgs Audio v2's results are our reevaluations. MOSS-TTS-v1.5's Seed-TTS result and the CosyVoice3/VoxCPM2 results are compiled in the [VoxCPM repository](https://github.com/OpenBMB/VoxCPM). Cross-project SIM values are omitted because speaker encoders and evaluation conventions differ. > **Parameter conventions:** Audio8's 0.6B excludes its separate codec; Qwen and CosyVoice use release labels; Higgs Audio v3 uses its nominal **4B** release label. The remaining sizes are rounded checkpoint counts used in our report (VoxCPM2 excludes its separate AudioVAE). These counts use different conventions across systems. ### Seed-TTS detail | Split | Metric | Preview error % ↓ | Realistic error % ↓ | Preview SIM ↑ | Realistic SIM ↑ | |---|---|---:|---:|---:|---:| | English | WER | 1.506 | 1.464 | 0.632 | 0.663 | | Chinese | CER | 0.950 | 1.029 | 0.731 | 0.745 | | Chinese, hard | CER | 11.510 | 12.797 | 0.687 | 0.702 | > **Note:** Preview values are from its [published Seed-TTS table](https://huggingface.co/Edge0/Audio8-TTS-Preview-0.6b#seed-tts), with SIM converted to a 0–1 scale. ### Multilingual detail

Audio8 TTS Preview supports multilingual speech generation and zero-shot voice cloning. This repository contains the complete checkpoint, its 44.1 kHz neural audio codec, tokenizer, processor, and Hugging Face remote code. > **Preview status:** Language coverage is intentionally limited in this > release. Cantonese  ·  Chinese  ·  Dutch  ·  English
French  ·  German  ·  Italian  ·  Japanese
Korean  ·  Polish  ·  Spanish

## Model Details Audio8 TTS uses a DualAR architecture inspired by [Fish Audio S2 Pro](https://github.com/fishaudio/fish-speech). Review the files in this repository, then load it with `trust_remote_code=True`. ### Zero-shot voice cloning The reference transcript must match the spoken content in the reference audio. ```python import soundfile as sf import torch from transformers import AutoModel, AutoProcessor model_id = "Audio8/Audio8-TTS-Preview-0.6b" device = "cuda" if torch.cuda.is_available() else "cpu" dtype = torch.bfloat16 if device == "cuda" else torch.float32 processor = AutoProcessor.from_pretrained(model_id, trust_remote_code=True) model = AutoModel.from_pretrained( model_id, trust_remote_code=True, dtype=dtype, ).eval().to(device) inputs = processor( text=["Welcome to Audio8 TTS."], reference_audio=["reference.wav"], reference_text=["The exact transcript of the reference recording."], return_tensors="pt", ) inputs = {name: value.to(device) for name, value in inputs.items()} with torch.inference_mode(): output = model.generate( **inputs, max_new_tokens=1024, temperature=0.8, top_p=0.95, top_k=50, do_sample=True, return_dict_in_generate=True, ) waveforms, waveform_lengths = model.decode_audio(output.codes) audio = waveforms[0, : int(waveform_lengths[0])].float().cpu().numpy() sf.write("output.wav", audio, model.config.codec_sample_rate) ``` ### Generation without a reference Omit `reference_audio` and `reference_text` when a cloned voice is not needed: ```python inputs = processor( text=["This utterance does not use a reference voice."], return_tensors="pt", ) ``` For command-line inference, batching, and supervised fine-tuning, see the [Audio8 TTS repository](https://github.com/Audio8-AI/Audio8_TTS). ## Deployment Options ### CPU deployment: ONNX INT4 [Audio8-TTS-Preview-0.6B-ONNX-INT4](https://huggingface.co/Audio8/Audio8-TTS-Preview-0.6B-ONNX-INT4) packages Audio8 TTS for low-resource CPU inference with ONNX Runtime. Slow and Fast AR weights use weight-only INT4, while activations, KV caches, and the neural audio codec use FP16. | Advantage | Details | |---|---| | CPU native | Runs with ONNX Runtime `CPUExecutionProvider`; no CUDA required | | Low memory | About **1 GiB after loading** in the tested Apple M2 configuration | | Small runtime | No PyTorch or Transformers dependency after model download | | Complete workflow | CLI, web and HTTP service, streaming PCM, and voice registration | Normal synthesis loads only the Slow AR, Fast AR, and codec decoder sessions. Voice registration releases those sessions before loading the optional codec encoder, keeping peak memory controlled. Get the [ONNX INT4 model](https://huggingface.co/Audio8/Audio8-TTS-Preview-0.6B-ONNX-INT4) and follow the [CPU ONNX Runtime guide](https://github.com/Audio8-AI/Audio8_TTS/tree/master/onnx_runtime). ### High-throughput serving: SGLang Omni Audio8 TTS now includes an [SGLang Omni adapter](https://github.com/Audio8-AI/Audio8_TTS/tree/master/sglang_omni) for production-oriented GPU serving. It is installed as an independent model plugin and does not overwrite SGLang Omni core files. | Capability | Support | |---|---| | Attention and batching | SGLang paged attention and dynamic batching | | DualAR execution | Slow AR serving with a fixed KV cache for the Fast AR codebook decoder | | Voice cloning | Reference-audio encoding and waveform decoding | | API | OpenAI-compatible `/v1/audio/speech` service | The released adapter is validated against a pinned SGLang Omni revision and supports both generation without a reference and zero-shot voice cloning. See the [SGLang Omni deployment guide](https://github.com/Audio8-AI/Audio8_TTS/tree/master/sglang_omni) for tested versions, installation, server configuration, and API examples. ## Evaluation Audio8 TTS Preview is the smallest model in this comparison at just **0.6B parameters**. Despite using only a fraction of the parameters of the other systems, it delivers results in the first tier of industry-leading SOTA TTS models on the benchmarks below. In particular, it achieves the best English WER and competitive Chinese CER on Seed-TTS, while remaining competitive across the CV3 multilingual evaluation. Lower WER/CER is better; higher SIM is better. Seed-TTS similarity values are shown as percentages. ### Seed-TTS | Model | Parameters | EN WER / SIM | ZH CER / SIM | Hard ZH CER / SIM | |---|---:|---:|---:|---:| | **Audio8 TTS Preview** | **0.6B** | **1.506** / 63.2 | 0.950 / 73.1 | 11.510 / 68.7 | | Fish S2 Pro | 4.6B | 1.607 / 64.6 | 1.038 / 73.8 | 10.149 / 70.1 | | Higgs Audio v2 | 4.7B | 1.524 / 66.4 | **0.806** / 72.1 | 10.622 / 69.3 | | CosyVoice3-1.5B | 1.5B | 2.22 / 72.0 | 1.12 / 78.1 | **5.83** / **75.8** | | MOSS-TTS | 8.5B | 1.85 / 73.4 | 1.20 / 78.8 | - | | VoxCPM2 | 2.3B | 1.84 / **75.3** | 0.97 / **79.5** | 8.13 / 75.3 | ### CV3 multilingual error rate | Model | Parameters | zh | en | hard-zh | hard-en | ja | ko | de | es | fr | it | ru | |---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:| | **Audio8 TTS Preview** | **0.6B** | **3.205** | **3.128** | 10.535 | 5.997 | 7.205 | 4.223 | 3.447 | 3.641 | 8.790 | 4.790 | - | | Fish S2 Pro | 4.6B | 3.600 | 3.493 | 10.588 | 7.349 | 5.139 | **4.111** | 3.605 | 2.972 | **8.600** | 4.229 | **4.702** | | Higgs Audio v2 | 4.7B | 3.378 | 3.404 | 10.424 | **5.754** | **4.742** | 4.260 | **3.300** | **2.929** | 9.425 | **3.555** | 5.423 | | CosyVoice3-1.5B | 1.5B | 3.91 | 4.99 | 9.77 | 10.55 | 7.57 | 5.69 | 6.43 | 4.47 | 11.8 | 10.5 | 6.64 | | VoxCPM2 | 2.3B | 3.65 | 5.00 | **8.55** | 8.48 | 5.96 | 5.69 | 4.77 | 3.80 | 9.85 | 4.25 | 5.21 | Parameter counts are calculated directly from the released weight tensors. It turns speech into two streams of integer tokens and decodes them back to 24 kHz audio. It was trained mostly on English and 10 Indian languages, and it is strongest on Indian languages: among codecs at about 1 kbps, it keeps the most words in every one of the 10 we tested. ## Key features - **Low bitrate:** 1.09 kbps, 75 tokens per second. - **Two token streams:** a content stream (25 Hz) that carries the words, and an acoustic stream (50 Hz) that carries the voice and detail. - **Split FSQ, not RVQ:** each stream is a single FSQ grid. Content is coded first, and one acoustic grid codes what remains, instead of a stack of residual codebooks. Each frame is one id per stream, with no learned codebook. - **16 kHz in, 24 kHz out:** any input sample rate is resampled to 16 kHz. - **One file:** all weights are in `model.safetensors`. Nothing else is downloaded. - **Commercial use allowed:** Apache 2.0. All training data is under open licences, none of them non-commercial. ## Model details | | | |---|---| | Content stream | 25 Hz, FSQ 8 × 3 levels = 6,561 ids, 317 bps | | Acoustic stream | 50 Hz, FSQ 6 × 6 levels = 46,656 ids, 775 bps | | Bitrate | 1.09 kbps | | Parameters | 624 M in the file, 387 M of them w2v-BERT 2.0; decoding alone uses 186 M | | Licence | Apache 2.0 | The content stream quantises w2v-BERT 2.0 features (layer 16). The acoustic stream quantises what a CNN encoder hears beyond the content stream. A transformer decoder with an iSTFT head turns the sum back into audio. IndiCodec is built on [NeuCodec](https://huggingface.co/neuphonic/neucodec) by Neuphonic: it uses NeuCodec's architecture, and training started from its released weights. The two-stream quantiser, the encoder training and the training recipe are new. ## Quality Speech codecs at about 1 kbps, on speakers not seen in training. Every codec is scored on the same clips. PESQ-WB (higher is better): | Test set | IndiCodec
1.09 kbps | Mimi, 8 codebooks
1.10 kbps | SNAC 24 kHz

0.80 kbps | |---|---|---|---|---| | LibriTTS-R test (English) | **2.41** | 2.32 | 2.29 | 2.19 | | CMU-Arctic (English) | **2.30** | 2.28 | 2.17 | 2.06 | | Seed-TTS eval (English) | 1.99 | **2.07** | 1.82 | 1.81 | | FLEURS, 10 Indian languages | **1.90** | 1.84 | 1.69 | 1.69 | Words after a round trip (lower is better): | | IndiCodec | Mimi | SNAC | NeuCodec | |---|---|---|---|---| | English WER, Seed-TTS eval | **2.5 %** | 3.6 % | 4.9 % | 3.5 % | | English WER, CMU-Arctic | **2.3 %** | 3.2 % | 3.8 % | 2.8 % | | Indian-language CER, FLEURS, 10 languages | **6.3 %** | 14.3 % | 13.3 % | 8.9 % | | Tokens per second | 75 | 100 | 82 | 50 | English WER uses Whisper large-v3. Indian-language CER uses the IndicConformer 600M ASR; the original recordings score 5.2 %, so IndiCodec adds 1.0 point. The 10 languages are Hindi, Bengali, Gujarati, Kannada, Malayalam, Marathi, Odia, Punjabi, Tamil and Telugu. ## Use ```bash hf download prakharkhatri/IndiCodec --local-dir IndiCodec && cd IndiCodec pip install torch==2.6.0 torchaudio==2.6.0 safetensors soundfile transformers==4.51.* vector-quantize-pytorch==1.17.8 torchtune==0.5.0 torchao==0.9.0 local-attention einops librosa pip install --no-deps "git+https://github.com/neuphonic/neucodec@ed3e6cd" ``` ```python import soundfile as sf from indicodec import IndiCodec codec = IndiCodec.load("model.safetensors") wav, sr = sf.read("speech.wav") content, acoustic = codec.encode(wav, sr) # token arrays audio = codec.decode(content, acoustic) # 24 kHz ``` ## Training data English: Emilia-YODAS (English part only), LibriTTS, LibriTTS-R and VCTK. Indian languages: Rasa, IndicVoices-R and IndicVoices from AI4Bharat. Plus about 15 h of laughs, sighs and coughs from VocalSound. All CC BY 4.0, except VocalSound (CC BY-SA 4.0). No audio is included in this release. ## Limits - Speech only; not for music. - Not streaming: the encoder and the decoder both attend over the whole clip. ## Licence Apache 2.0. # Drama 3 8-bit, paged for gbx-lm

**Built with Fish Audio.** [Fish Audio Drama 3](https://huggingface.co/fishaudio/drama-3), the expressive multi-speaker text-to-speech model, packaged for [gbx-lm](https://github.com/GreenBitAI/gbx-lm) on Apple silicon: an OpenAI-compatible `/v1/audio/speech` server that streams audio, and runs on Macs that cannot hold the whole model in memory.

This is a community build by GreenBitAI. It is not made, sponsored or endorsed by Fish Audio.

- **Where the weights come from.** Fish Audio's release, as converted to MLX 8-bit by [mlx-community/fish-audio-drama-3-8bit](https://huggingface.co/mlx-community/fish-audio-drama-3-8bit) (routed experts 8-bit, everything else as released). This repository changes how those weights are laid out on disk, not their values: the routed experts move into `experts.bin`, one record per expert, so that a machine can read just the experts it needs. Checked when the repository was built, against the mlx-community weights: identical output up to 127-token prompts, and every layer identical.
- **Real time on 64 GB and up.** 46-47 frames per second on an M3 Ultra, 2.2x real time, first audio in under 0.3 s when streaming.
- **Runs on 32-48 GB, for offline use.** With less memory the experts stream from the SSD: about half real time on a 48 GB Mac, a third on 32 GB. Generate the file, then play it.

## What you need

| | |
|---|---|
| Mac | Apple silicon; 64 GB or more for real time, 32 GB at least |
| Disk | 40 GB for the model |
| gbx-lm | a release with speech support |
| Python | 3.10 or newer, for the audio codec (below) |

gbx-lm generates the model's audio *codes*; turning codes into sound is the job of a small companion package, [gbx-codecs](https://github.com/GreenBitAI/gbx-codecs), which gbx-lm starts in its own process. It needs only `mlx`, `numpy` and `miniaudio` -- no PyTorch, no ffmpeg -- and about 3 GB of memory while it decodes. The codec weights are in this repository.

## Setup

**1. gbx-lm.** The prebuilt binary, as in the [gbx-lm README](https://github.com/GreenBitAI/gbx-lm):

```bash
curl -fL -o gbx_lm-darwin-arm64.tar.gz 'https://github.com/GreenBitAI/gbx-lm/releases/latest/download/gbx_lm-darwin-arm64.tar.gz' \
  && tar -xzf gbx_lm-darwin-arm64.tar.gz gbx_lm
```

**2. The codec**, in a virtual environment of its own (this location is the one gbx-lm looks in by default):

```bash
python3 -m venv ~/.gbx-codecs
~/.gbx-codecs/bin/pip install gbx-codecs
```

**3. Voices (optional).** To speak in a particular voice, put a short clean recording (5-30 s; wav, flac or mp3) and its exact transcript side by side in a folder:

```
~/voices/
    narrator.wav
    narrator.txt      # the words spoken in narrator.wav
```

The request's `voice` is the file name, `narrator`. Use only voices you have the right to use -- see [License](#license). Without a voice (`"voice": "default"`) the model chooses one; fix it with a `seed`.

**4. Start the server.** The model downloads on first start:

```bash
./gbx_lm --model GreenBitAI/Drama-3-8bit-paged --voices_dir ~/voices
```

If the codec is not in `~/.gbx-codecs`, add `--codec_python /path/to/that/python`. To check the codec on its own once the model is downloaded:

```bash
~/.gbx-codecs/bin/gbx-codecs check ~/.libra/cache/models/hub/models--GreenBitAI--Drama-3-8bit-paged/snapshots/*/
```

## Use

```bash
curl http://127.0.0.1:11688/v1/audio/speech -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{
  "model": "GreenBitAI/Drama-3-8bit-paged",
  "input": "[sighs] Fine. If we miss the train, that is on you. [laughs] Okay, okay, I am going.",
  "voice": "narrator",
  "response_format": "wav"
}' -o out.wav
```

With the OpenAI SDK, streaming as it is generated:

```python
from openai import OpenAI

client = OpenAI(base_url="http://127.0.0.1:11688/v1", api_key="local")
with client.audio.speech.with_streaming_response.create(
    model="GreenBitAI/Drama-3-8bit-paged",
    voice="narrator",
    input="<|speaker:0|> Are you coming tonight? <|speaker:1|> I wouldn't miss it.",
    response_format="pcm",                # 24 kHz, 16-bit, mono
    extra_body={"stream_format": "audio", "seed": 7},
) as response:
    for chunk in response.iter_bytes():
        ...                               # play or write it
```

| field | |
|---|---|
| `input` | the text. Inline cues such as `[laughs]`, `[sighs]`, `[whispering]`; speakers `<|speaker:0|>` to `<|speaker:15|>`. Long text is split and spoken in order |
| `voice` | a name from `--voices_dir`, or `default` |
| `response_format` | `wav` (44.1 kHz, the default) or `pcm` (24 kHz, as OpenAI's). Other formats are refused |
| `stream_format` | `audio` to stream; absent, the whole file is returned |
| `seed`, `temperature`, `top_p`, `sample_rate` | extensions; from the OpenAI SDK, pass them in `extra_body` |

`speed` other than 1.0 and `instructions` are not supported by this model: emotion and delivery come from the inline cues.

Pauses longer than a second are shortened in the output: the model occasionally goes silent mid-sentence for many seconds before finishing it.

## Quality

32 texts in English and Chinese (plain, cued, two-speaker, and long enough to be split), one take each, transcribed by Whisper large-v3-turbo:

| | English word error | Chinese character error |
|---|---|---|
| mlx-audio reference implementation, mlx-community 8-bit | 0.0% | 1.1-1.5% |
| this repository on gbx-lm, in memory | 0.0-0.1% | 1.3% |
| this repository on gbx-lm, streaming experts | 0.1% | 1.3% |

No take had an error rate over 20%.

## Speed

M3 Ultra, experts read from a cold SSD where they stream; the model makes 21.5 frames for each second of audio:

| Mac | how | frames/s | x real time |
|---|---|---|---|
| 64 GB and up | in memory | 46-47 | 2.2 |
| 48 GB | streaming experts | 10-13 | 0.5-0.6 |
| 32 GB | streaming experts | 7-8.5 | 0.35-0.4 |

The smaller tiers are measured with the expert cache gbx-lm would give those Macs, on a Mac Studio's SSD; a laptop's is slower, so expect less. 24 GB Macs can load the model but run at under a quarter of real time. gbx-lm decides how to load the model from the memory it finds; `GBX_PAGING=off` forces it into memory.

## License

The [Fish Audio Community License, Version 1.0](LICENSE) applies to this model, including the outputs you make with it. In short, and the license itself governs:

- Free for research and non-commercial use, and for commercial use by organizations with annual revenue under USD 500,000. Above that, or to offer text-to-speech to third parties as a **hosted service** (an API or app whose purpose is speech generation from their text or voices), you need a separate license from Fish Audio (business@fish.audio).
- Do not generate speech imitating an identifiable person without their consent, impersonate anyone to deceive, or use the outputs to train other speech or foundation models.
- [NOTICE](NOTICE) records the attribution and every change made to Fish Audio's weights, including this repository's.

gbx-lm is Apache 2.0 and gbx-codecs is MIT. The codec implementation in gbx-codecs and the model implementation in gbx-lm are adapted from [mlx-audio](https://github.com/Blaizzy/mlx-audio) (MIT).

## Credits

Fish Audio for Drama 3. [cguldogan](https://github.com/cguldogan) for the MLX 8-bit conversion published as mlx-community/fish-audio-drama-3-8bit. Prince Canuma and the mlx-audio contributors for the MLX implementation this build and its codec are based on.

# Pocket TTS ONNX

ONNX export of [Pocket TTS](https://huggingface.co/kyutai/pocket-tts) for lightweight multilingual text-to-speech with zero-shot voice cloning.

## Model Description

Pocket TTS is a compact text-to-speech model from Kyutai that supports voice cloning from short audio samples. This ONNX export provides:

- **Zero-shot voice cloning** from any audio reference
- **Multilingual bundles** for `english_2026-04`, `french_24l`, `german`, `german_24l`, `italian`, `italian_24l`, `portuguese`, `portuguese_24l`, `spanish`, and `spanish_24l`
- **INT8 quantized models** for fast CPU inference
- **Streaming support** with adaptive chunking for real-time playback
- **Temperature control** for generation diversity
- **Dual model architecture** for flexible flow matching

## Architecture

This export uses a **dual model split** for the Flow LM:

```
flow_lm_main   - Transformer/conditioner (produces conditioning vectors)
flow_lm_flow   - Flow network only (Euler integration for latent sampling)
```

This architecture enables:
- **Temperature control**: Adjust generation diversity via noise scaling
- **Variable LSD steps**: Trade off speed vs quality
- **External flow loop**: Full control over the sampling process

## Performance

Performance depends on the selected language bundle, precision, CPU, and `lsd_steps`.

- 6-layer bundles such as `english_2026-04`, `german`, `italian`, `portuguese`, and `spanish` are much smaller and faster than the `*_24l` bundles.
- INT8 bundles substantially reduce `flow_lm_main`, `flow_lm_flow`, and `mimi_decoder` size for CPU inference.
- `mimi_encoder.onnx` and `text_conditioner.onnx` remain FP32.

### Optimized Inference

Thread count is automatically tuned to avoid over-subscription on the small sequential matmuls in the autoregressive loop (`intra_op_num_threads=min(cpu_count, 4)`, `inter_op_num_threads=1`). This alone provides a **~2x speedup** over default ORT settings on multi-core machines.

### Decoding Strategy

- **Offline (`generate`)**: Uses **threaded parallel decoding** — the mimi decoder runs in a background thread, decoding 12-frame chunks while the flow loop generates the next frames. This overlaps generation and decoding for maximum throughput.
- **Streaming (`stream`)**: Uses **adaptive chunking** (starts at 2 frames). This ensures instant start (low TTFB) while scaling up chunk sizes for throughput.

## Usage

```python
from pocket_tts_onnx import PocketTTSOnnx

# Load the English bundle (INT8 by default)
tts = PocketTTSOnnx(
    models_dir="onnx",
    language="english_2026-04",
)

# Generate speech with built-in voice state
audio = tts.generate(
    text="Hello, this is a test.",
    voice="alba",
)

# Generate speech with voice cloning from audio
audio = tts.generate(
    text="Hello, this is a test of voice cloning.",
    voice="reference_sample.wav"
)

# Save output
tts.save_audio(audio, "output.wav")
```

### Temperature Control

Adjust generation diversity with the `temperature` parameter:

```python
# More deterministic (lower temperature)
tts = PocketTTSOnnx(temperature=0.3)

# Default balance
tts = PocketTTSOnnx(temperature=0.7)

# More diverse/expressive (higher temperature)
tts = PocketTTSOnnx(temperature=1.0)
```

### LSD Steps

Trade off speed vs quality with `lsd_steps`:

```python
# Default
tts = PocketTTSOnnx(lsd_steps=1)

# Slower, potentially smoother
tts = PocketTTSOnnx(lsd_steps=4)
```

### Streaming Mode

For real-time applications with low time-to-first-audio:

```python
for chunk in tts.stream("Hello world!", voice="reference_sample.wav"):
    play_audio(chunk)  # Process each chunk as it arrives
```

### Language Bundles

```python
# German bundle with built-in voice
tts = PocketTTSOnnx(language="german", precision="fp32")
audio = tts.generate("Hallo zusammen. Dies ist ein deutscher Test.", voice="alba")
```

Built-in voice names are loaded from each bundle's metadata. Voice cloning also accepts:

- a reference audio path
- a `.safetensors` prompt-state file
- a precomputed embedding array

### Legacy Layout

Root-level files under `onnx/` and the root `tokenizer.model` are still present for backward compatibility with older integrations that expect the original single-model layout.

New integrations should use the per-language bundle directories under `onnx/<language>/`.

### Command Line

```bash
python generate.py "Hello, this is a test." alba output.wav --language english_2026-04
python generate.py "Hallo zusammen." samples/reference.wav output.wav --language german --precision fp32
```
