# MOSS-TTS v1.5 — GPTQPro4-Fused

**Project preference: GPTQ Pro fused.** The owner preferred this runtime after reviewing the audio. This is a subjective project choice, not evidence that it wins every objective score. The fused Triton range guard is part of the tested runtime; it uses the same packed weights as the normal GPTQ adapter and generated byte-identical WAVs for all 16 matched cases.

This is a **native custom checkpoint**, with measured RTX 3090 audio results and a successful fresh-install RTX 3060 GPU audio test. It requires the supplied runtime adapter and the pinned GPTQ-Pro backend. It is **not** a standard AutoGPTQ/Transformers checkpoint or a drop-in file for llama.cpp, vLLM, or an unmodified EXL3 model loader. Review the custom Python code before running it.

## Findings

| Runtime | Synthesis RTF | Peak allocated / reserved GiB | WavLM | ECAPA | Predicted UTMOS | CER / WER |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| BF16 | 0.558 | 19.50 / 19.91 | 0.9703 | 0.6210 | 3.126 | 1.13% / 3.25% |
| AWQ4-G64 | 1.212 | 10.66 / 11.07 | 0.9685 | 0.5807 | 3.177 | 1.63% / 4.27% |
| GPTQPro4 | 0.759 | 10.04 / 10.50 | 0.9694 | 0.6119 | 3.120 | 2.14% / 5.69% |
| GPTQPro4-Fused | 0.605 | 10.04 / 10.48 | 0.9694 | 0.6119 | 3.120 | 2.14% / 5.69% |
| EXL3-4 | 0.518 | 9.79 / 9.84 | 0.9652 | 0.6135 | 3.127 | 2.18% / 4.88% |
| EXL3-5 | 0.525 | 10.56 / 10.62 | 0.9721 | 0.6405 | 3.111 | 1.13% / 3.66% |

RTF is synthesis time divided by resulting audio duration; it includes actual co-resident FP32 decoding. Lower RTF and memory are better. WavLM/ECAPA are cosines against original reference recordings, not percentages. UTMOS is predicted naturalness, not human MOS. CER/WER measure generated-audio intelligibility through Whisper-small and include recognizer errors.

There are 16 cases per runtime: two existing female reference voices, three Spanish prompts and one English prompt, two seeds (1234 and 501). Total: 96 render records, 80 unique WAV hashes; the two GPTQ runtimes are not independent audio samples. References were 15 s and 11.008 s and were not recordings of the intended callers. All five UTMOS folds, original-reference WavLM/ECAPA with alternate-voice controls, finite audio, EOS and hashes were verified. Each native quantization checked 252 modules against its reconstructed quantized weights, minimum cosine at least 0.999; that is native-kernel parity, not BF16 equivalence.

EXL3-5 measured in a later GPU window, with other-GPU activity. Small timing differences are not controlled speed evidence. The tested AWQ path dequantizes to BF16 GEMM; it is not an optimized Marlin result. Do not generalize that timing to every AWQ implementation.

**English remains a screening concern.** Only four cases and one English prompt per runtime were tested. Predicted English UTMOS: BF16 3.323, GPTQ 3.137, EXL3-4 3.078, EXL3-5 3.090. English CER: BF16 0%, GPTQ/EXL3-4 4.55%, EXL3-5 1.82%. Validate both languages with the actual callers and blinded listening. Higher mean reference cosine does not establish a universal identity or quality winner.

## Fresh-install RTX 3060 result

A clean Python 3.12 environment, anonymous public checkpoint download and newly compiled native GPTQ Pro extension generated all 16 matched clips successfully on a 12 GB RTX 3060. Pooled generation/synthesis RTF: **1.535 / 1.552**; peak allocated/reserved VRAM: **10.040 / 10.480 GiB**. The earlier 3090 synthesis RTF was 0.605: this 3060 host used **2.567 times** as much timed synthesis per second of audio and did not sustain real time.

Short Spanish cases averaged 4.56 s audio, available as complete utterances after 9.12 s of timed synthesis. The host CPU was an i7-4790; CPU, GPU and measurement-window differences are part of this comparison. All 16 WAV hashes differ from the 3090 outputs, so earlier quality scores are not assigned to the new audio. Streaming, simultaneous calls and 3060 quality rescoring were not tested. [Fresh-install procedure and caveats](FRESH-INSTALL-3060.md), [per-clip metrics](benchmark/3060-fresh-install-20261027.json).

## Format and tensor allocation

All 252 transformer linears at 4 bits; text embedding and all 33 heads affine 8-bit G64; audio embeddings/norms original BF16.

GPTQ uses native symmetric W4/G64 and FP16 kernel scales, with a per-row power-of-two input guard and FP32 restoration to BF16. This publication uses the fused Triton guard. EXL3 uses native calibrated LDLQ trellis coding with no affine group-64 or zero-point equivalent. The same backbone tensors are selected; quantized distributions and algorithms differ. Weights were converted directly from pinned BF16, never by requantizing AWQ or EXL3-4.

Weight SHA-256: `e48be4962999023b7a57601b301385b0a02d5452b4ea72e4f5e48fdf6febcc37`. Tensor payload: 5,516,332,016 bytes; effective 5.1981 bits per original parameter including protected tensors. Safetensors container size is slightly larger.

Only the generator checkpoint is distributed. Download the original FP32 codec separately at revision `3cd226ba2947efa357ef453bcad111b6eafba782`; generator and codec both contribute to reported VRAM. The MOSS checkpoint has no compatible trained MTP path; its 33 text/RVQ heads are not future-token predictors. Matched W4A8 was not tested because the installed QQQ kernel lacks G64 support.

## Download and verify

```python
from huggingface_hub import snapshot_download
model_dir = snapshot_download("groxaxo/MOSS-TTS-v1.5-GPTQ-Pro-4bit-Fused")
```

Run `python verify_bundle.py` inside the snapshot to verify all distributed file hashes and checkpoint structure. This does not execute CUDA or rerun unavailable private-reference media.

## Native runtime

The measured environment is listed in [tested-environment.txt](tested-environment.txt): Linux, Python 3.12, Torch 2.11.0+cu130, Transformers 5.19.0 and Triton 3.6.0 on one RTX 3090. EXL3 compilation used CUDA toolkit 12.8. Install the pinned backend using its own build instructions:

- GPTQ-Pro: [groxaxo/GPTQ-Pro](https://github.com/groxaxo/GPTQ-Pro/tree/c02dd675ad74cec2cc79f654d3c135ac225c8e23), import `gptqmodel`.
- EXL3: [turboderp-org/exllamav3](https://github.com/turboderp-org/exllamav3/tree/02aef45cd681b960a00afcd0749a4ab99e6c1bfe), import `exllamav3`.

Install the dependency matching this model. No native binary is bundled. The loader uses its native packed modules plus protected affine embedding/heads; ordinary `AutoModel.from_pretrained` is not supported for these weights.

Download the codec:

```python
from huggingface_hub import snapshot_download
codec_dir = snapshot_download("OpenMOSS-Team/MOSS-Audio-Tokenizer", revision="3cd226ba2947efa357ef453bcad111b6eafba782")
print(codec_dir)
```

Then, from this model snapshot on a GPU you have reserved:

```bash
CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 python infer.py --codec-dir /path/to/codec --reference /path/to/consented-reference.wav --language Spanish --text "Hola, me alegra hablar con vos." --output output.wav
```

Use `--language English` for English text. The CLI encodes the reference with FP32, unloads the encoder, loads the native generator and FP32 decoder, then returns the complete waveform. **The public package passed a fresh-install RTX 3060 CUDA/audio smoke test on 27 October 2026, followed by 16 matched audio cases.** See [installation steps and limitations](FRESH-INSTALL-3060.md), including the documented NumPy dependency-metadata exception. This validates this tested installation; live-call deployment remains untested.

## Practical limits

Full-utterance RTF is not streaming time to first audio, simultaneous-speaker throughput or telephone latency. Actual two-way conversations, 30-second enrolment, physical iPhone audio routing, caller-specific resemblance and human preference tests remain unvalidated. Allow cold-start headroom: EXL3-5 setup/reload reporting reached 17.19 GiB allocated / 17.96 GiB reserved, above its 10.56 GiB synthesis peak. Do not assume ASR co-residency from isolated TTS numbers.

Use reference recordings with the speaker's permission. No voice WAVs, cached reference codes, speaker embeddings, calibration tensors, evaluator weights or credentials are in this repository. Recreating bit-identical quantization requires the original permitted calibration inputs, which are not distributed; their hashes and protocol are recorded.

[Grouped voice/language metrics](benchmark/grouped-quality.json), [per-clip metrics](benchmark/comparison.csv), [validation receipt](benchmark/completed-six-profile-verification.json), [model provenance](provenance.json). Machine identifiers/absolute paths were redacted from public metrics; numeric measurements are unchanged. The benchmark source archive at [experimentos, commit 4f9339c](https://github.com/groxaxo/experimentos/tree/4f9339cee124bf32aef089d0df3b9dde1c5f9bef/moss-tts-awq/voice-similarity-gptq-exl3-3090-2026-10-21) may require access; the relevant metric evidence is included here.

# OmniVoice — Azerbaijani

Azerbaijani text-to-speech model fine-tuned from [k2-fsa/OmniVoice](https://huggingface.co/k2-fsa/OmniVoice)
(Qwen3-0.6B backbone + Higgs Audio V2 codec, 24 kHz output). Supports zero-shot voice cloning from a short
reference clip as well as generation without any reference audio.

## Installation

```bash
pip install omnivoice soundfile
```

## Usage

### Load the model

```python
import soundfile as sf
import torch
from omnivoice import OmniVoice

device = "cuda:0" if torch.cuda.is_available() else "cpu"
dtype = torch.float16 if device != "cpu" else torch.float32

model = OmniVoice.from_pretrained(
    "LocalDoc/omnivoice-azerbaijani",
    device_map=device,
    dtype=dtype,
)
```

Runs on GPU (fp16) or CPU (fp32); CPU inference works but is noticeably slower.

### 1. With a reference voice (voice cloning)

Provide a clean 5–15 s reference recording and its exact transcript. The model reproduces the
speaker's timbre and speaking style.

```python
audio = model.generate(
    text="Salam, sizə necə kömək edə bilərəm?",
    ref_audio="ref.wav",
    ref_text="Referans səsin dəqiq mətni.",
    language="az",
    num_step=32,
)
sf.write("cloned.wav", audio[0], 24000)
```

If you synthesize many sentences with the same voice, build the prompt once and reuse it:

```python
prompt = model.create_voice_clone_prompt(
    ref_audio="ref.wav",
    ref_text="Referans səsin dəqiq mətni.",
)

sentences = [
    "Sifarişiniz qəbul olundu.",
    "Kartınız sabah hazır olacaq.",
]
audios = model.generate(
    text=sentences,
    voice_clone_prompt=prompt,
    language="az",
    num_step=32,
)
for i, a in enumerate(audios):
    sf.write(f"cloned_{i}.wav", a, 24000)
```

### 2. Without a reference voice

**Auto voice** — pass only the text; the model picks a voice itself:

```python
audio = model.generate(
    text="Bu gün hava günəşli olacaq.",
    language="az",
    num_step=32,
)
sf.write("auto.wav", audio[0], 24000)
```

**Voice design** — describe the desired voice with `instruct` (comma-separated attributes such as
`male` / `female`, `young adult` / `middle-aged` / `elderly`, `low pitch` / `high pitch`, `whisper`):

```python
audio = model.generate(
    text="Bu gün hava günəşli olacaq.",
    instruct="female, young adult, moderate pitch",
    language="az",
    num_step=32,
)
sf.write("designed.wav", audio[0], 24000)
```

Voice design comes from the base OmniVoice model; for a stable, consistent voice across many
utterances, voice cloning from a reference is recommended.

### Tips

- Write numbers, dates and abbreviations as words: the model expects normalized text
  (e.g. *iyirmi beş* instead of *25*).
- `num_step` trades speed for quality (32 is a good default; 16 is faster).
- Use `speed=` (e.g. `0.9`, `1.1`) or `duration=` (seconds) to control pacing.

## Limitations

- Numbers, dates and abbreviations must be written out as words.
- Voice cloning quality depends on the reference: use clean 5–15 s audio with an exact transcript.
- Without a reference, the voice may vary from call to call.

The base OmniVoice weights are released under CC BY-NC 4.0, so this fine-tune is **non-commercial**.

# maya-mac: Maya TTS on Apple Silicon

Run [maya-research/maya2-native](https://huggingface.co/maya-research/maya2-native) on a Mac. It covers 12 Indic languages
and English, has 21 built-in voices, and supports zero-shot voice cloning. The official `maya3` package needs an
NVIDIA GPU because it uses Triton kernels and CUDA graphs. This package is a rewrite of that inference path for Apple
Silicon: an [MLX](https://github.com/ml-explore/mlx) engine with custom Metal kernels (the default; ~3x faster than real
time on an M5 Pro, ~4x with 8-bit weights), and the original PyTorch MPS engine as a fallback.

This repo contains **code only**. The weights download from the original model repos the first time you run it
(~5.5 GB, cached by Hugging Face).

## Requirements

- Mac with Apple Silicon (M1 or newer), macOS 14+
- Python 3.10–3.12
- ~6 GB free disk
- RAM: tested on 24 GB. The MLX engine peaks at ~8.5 GB (fp16) or ~7 GB (`--bits 8`), so 16 GB Macs should work.

## Install

```bash
# pip (installs the prebuilt wheel from this repo):
pip install "maya-mac @ https://huggingface.co/justanurag/maya-mac/resolve/main/dist/maya_mac-0.3.0-py3-none-any.whl"

# or uv, straight from git (puts the `maya` command on your PATH):
uv tool install --python 3.12 "maya-mac @ git+https://huggingface.co/justanurag/maya-mac"
```

`pip install git+https://huggingface.co/...` does **not** work: the Hugging Face git server rejects the partial
clone that recent pip uses. Use the wheel URL above, or uv.

## Use

```bash
maya "नमस्ते, आपका ऑर्डर कल पहुँच जाएगा।" -l hi -v Ahana --normalize -o speech.wav
maya --list-voices
maya "Hello there." -l en --ref-audio me.wav --ref-text "exact transcript of me.wav"     # clone a voice
maya "Hello there." -l en --bits 8                     # 8-bit weights: ~1.4x faster again, see Speed
```

```python
import soundfile as sf
from maya_mac import MayaTTS

tts = MayaTTS.from_pretrained()          # first run downloads the weights; loads in ~10-20 s
wav = tts.generate("नमस्ते, आपका ऑर्डर कल पहुँच जाएगा।", lang="hi", voice="Ahana", normalize=True)
sf.write("speech.wav", wav, 24000)       # float32 mono, 24 kHz

for chunk in tts.stream("A long paragraph ...", lang="en", voice="Vaidehi"):   # 240 ms chunks as they are made
    ...

tts.register_voice("me", ref_audio="me.wav", ref_text="exact transcript", lang="en")
wav = tts.generate("धन्यवाद!", lang="hi", voice="me")       # the reference and output languages can differ
```

- **Languages:** `as bn en gu hi kn ml mr or pa ta te`
- **Sampling options:** `seed`, `temperature`, `top_k`, `top_p`, `repetition_penalty`
- **`normalize=True`:** expands numbers, currency, dates, URLs and similar written forms into spoken text.
- **Engine settings:** see `maya_mac.engine.EngineConfig`, and pass them as `from_pretrained(**settings)`. The MLX
  engine is used whenever MLX is installed on Apple Silicon; `backend="torch"` (or `device="mps"`) selects the
  PyTorch engine, and `backbone_bits=8, depth_bits=8` the 8-bit weights.
- **Local weights:** set `MAYA_MODEL_DIR` to a folder holding `maya2-native/`, `mimi/` and `ecapa/` to use those
  instead of downloading.

Only clone a voice with the speaker's permission. See the
[original model card](https://huggingface.co/maya-research/maya2-native) for intended use and limitations.

## Server

`maya-server` runs a server for other apps to use. It has an OpenAI-compatible speech endpoint and WebSocket
streaming, and uses the same protocol as the upstream `maya3` server, so existing maya3 clients and OpenAI-style TTS
clients work unchanged.

```bash
maya-server --port 8080            # first run downloads the weights; GET /health turns 200 when ready
maya-server --port 8080 --bits 8   # 8-bit weights

curl -s localhost:8080/v1/audio/speech -H 'content-type: application/json' \
  -d '{"input": "नमस्ते, आप कैसे हैं?", "voice": "Ahana", "response_format": "mp3"}' -o hello.mp3
```

| Endpoint | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `POST /v1/audio/speech` | OpenAI-compatible; `response_format` wav / pcm / mp3 / opus (streamed) or flac; `stream_format: "sse"`; `language` (guessed from the script if absent), `voice`, `normalize`, `seed`, `temperature`, `top_k`, `top_p`, `repetition_penalty`, `max_frames` |
| `WS /v1/tts/stream` | Low-latency PCM streaming: `speak` / `cancel` / `ping` messages, several contexts per socket |
| `GET/POST /v1/voices`, `DELETE /v1/voices/{id}` | List voices, clone one from a wav (multipart `ref_audio` + `ref_text` + `lang`), remove it |
| `GET /health`, `GET /v1/models` | Readiness and stats; model list |

```python
from maya_mac.client import Maya3Client
Maya3Client("http://127.0.0.1:8080").speech("Hello there.", "out.wav", language="en", voice="Kayal")
```

**Requests run one at a time** in arrival order. The upstream server batches dozens of requests on one NVIDIA GPU,
but this one doesn't batch. If a request is still waiting for its first audio after `--queue-deadline-ms` (default
30 s), or more than `--max-pending` requests (default 4) are already waiting, the server refuses it with 503 /
`overloaded`. A client that disconnects or cancels frees the engine within about a quarter of a second. The server
listens on `127.0.0.1` by default; pass `--host 0.0.0.0` to expose it on your network.

## Speed (M5 Pro, 24 GB)

Measured back to back on the same machine, on battery in High Power mode. Real-time factor = generation time / audio
duration, so lower is faster.

| | torch MPS | MLX fp16 (default) | MLX `--bits 8` |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Real-time factor, 21 s paragraph | 0.77 | 0.32 | 0.23 |
| Real-time factor, short sentences | 0.77–0.80 | 0.33 | 0.23 |
| Time per 80 ms frame | ~63 ms | 26.4 ms | 18.8 ms |
| First audio | 0.31–0.39 s | 0.16–0.18 s | 0.12–0.14 s |
| Load time, including warm-up (weights cached) | ~12 s | ~1 s | ~1 s |
| Whisper-small CER en / hi (18 utterances each) | 6.4 / 16.3 % | 6.4 / 16.3 % | 7.0 / 13.3 % |

In Low Power Mode the GPU drops to about half its clock after a second of sustained load, and the paragraph's
real-time factor becomes 1.41 / 0.63 / 0.44.

The fp16 engine computes the same function as the torch engine: against the model in fp32 its hidden states, cb0 logits
and depth logits are within 0.1–0.25 % (torch MPS fp16: ~0.4 %). 8-bit weights move the logits by ~2–3 %, about as much
as bf16 does; transcription error is unchanged within noise. `tests/test_mlx_parity.py` checks both.

## How it works

Model, prompt format, sampler, stop rule and guards are the same as upstream. This is the inference code only.

Per 80 ms frame the engine runs one Qwen3-1.7B decode step and then a 31-level depth decoder, i.e. 124 tiny transformer
layer passes, each depending on the one before. At one stream that is bound by memory bandwidth (~6 GB of weights read
per frame in fp16) and by the latency of dependent GPU kernels, not by FLOPs, so the engine is built to read fewer bytes
and launch fewer kernels:

- **MLX instead of PyTorch MPS.** MLX's fused Metal kernels (`rms_norm`, `rope`, `scaled_dot_product_attention`,
  quantized matmul) and lazy graphs, with no per-op Python dispatch for the depth decoder: the cb0 sampler, all 31 depth
  levels and the feedback embedding are one `mx.compile`d graph.
- **Custom Metal kernels for the depth decoder** (`mlx_kernels.py`). A layer pass goes from ~12 dependent kernels to 5:
  LayerNorm folded into the matvec (one pass, no barrier), GELU / residual / speaker-constant epilogues, KV append +
  causal attention in one kernel, and top-k (exact radix select) + Gumbel-max draw + next-level embedding in one kernel.
  The fp16 depth step drops from ~27 ms to ~16-21 ms.
- **Pipelined frames.** Frame t+1 is queued on the GPU before the host reads frame t (stop flag + 32 codes, one read),
  so guards and the hand-off to Mimi overlap GPU work. A speculative frame is dropped when frame t stops, and recomputed
  when the loop guard changes the AEOS bias, so the output is what the sequential loop would produce.
- **Voice prefix KV cache.** A cloned voice's reference clip is prefilled once; later requests restore its KV and only
  prefill their own text.
- **Optional 8-bit weights** for the backbone and the depth decoder: about half the bytes per frame.

| Module | What it is |
| --- | --- |
| `engine.py` | One request at a time: prompt → backbone → first-code sampling and stop rule → depth decoder → feedback. Also the duration and loop guards, text splitting and voices; picks the backend |
| `mlx_engine.py` | The MLX engine (`MayaMLX`, a `MayaTTS`): pipelined frame loop, voice prefix cache, all MLX work on one thread it owns |
| `mlx_model.py` | The model in MLX, loaded straight from the release safetensors: Qwen3 backbone, compiled frame step (cb0 sampler, depth decoder, feedback), prompt composition |
| `mlx_kernels.py` | Custom Metal kernels for the depth decoder: LayerNorm + matvec + epilogues (fp16 / 8-bit), tiny causal attention, top-k sampler |
| `fast_backbone.py`, `fast_depth.py` | The PyTorch MPS engine's lean backbone and depth decoder |
| `codec.py` | Streaming Mimi decoder; runs on the CPU in a worker thread |
| `serving.py` | Queued engine for the server: one worker thread owns the model, runs requests in order, and handles cancellation and voice registration |
| `server.py`, `client.py` | Upstream maya3 server and client, unchanged protocol, wired to `serving.py` |
| `tts/`, `prompt.py`, `guards.py`, `text/`, `reference.py`, `configs/` | Vendored from [MayaResearch/maya2-native](https://github.com/MayaResearch/maya2-native) (Apache-2.0, `LICENSE.upstream`) |

MLX findings (0.32.4):

- Streams are thread-local: arrays and compiled graphs built on one thread fail on another ("There is no Stream(gpu, 1)
  in current thread"). The engine therefore does all MLX work on one thread of its own.
- `audio_in.norm` is `nn.RMSNorm(eps=None)`, whose epsilon follows the input dtype (fp16: 9.8e-4). That is ~35 % of a
  feedback frame's mean square, so the MLX engine uses the same epsilon rather than a fixed one.
- A one-pass matvec kernel that re-reads its input rows is fine for a few positions and 7x slower than MLX's tiled
  GEMM at 18-26 positions, so the long first passes of the depth bands use MLX's matmul.

MPS findings with torch 2.8.0:

- `scaled_dot_product_attention` returns wrong attention for this backbone in fp16/bf16 (~95 % relative error), so
  the model babbles or stops early. The backbone uses its own attention, which is within 0.4 % of fp32.
- HF's Qwen3 RMSNorm takes 133 µs per call on MPS, and `F.rms_norm` takes 6 µs for the same output.
- Indexing with a 0-dim device tensor forces a host sync (~0.7 ms). `F.embedding` avoids it.

## Tests

```bash
uv run --group dev pytest tests/                                  # Metal kernels vs MLX ops (no weights needed)
MAYA_MODEL_DIR=models uv run --group dev pytest tests/            # + MLX vs torch fp32 parity on the real weights
```

# Russian Emotional TTS (350M DiT / Flow Matching)

[![Download Colab Notebook](https://img.shields.io/badge/Colab%20Notebook-Download%20.ipynb-blue?logo=googlecolab)](https://huggingface.co/Andreevai/f5-tts-russian-emotional/resolve/main/russian_emotional_tts_colab.ipynb)

An advanced Russian Text-to-Speech (TTS) and voice cloning model based on the **DiT (Diffusion Transformer) / Flow-Matching** architecture (F5-TTS). Fine-tuned on high-fidelity, expressive theatrical dialogues with lexical stress annotation.

### 🚀 Quick Online Demo (Google Colab Free GPU)
1. Download the notebook: [russian_emotional_tts_colab.ipynb](https://huggingface.co/Andreevai/f5-tts-russian-emotional/resolve/main/russian_emotional_tts_colab.ipynb)
2. Go to [Google Colab](https://colab.research.google.com/) -> Click **Upload** -> select the downloaded file.
3. Switch runtime to **T4 GPU** (Runtime -> Change runtime type -> T4 GPU) and run all cells.
4. Open the generated `gradio.live` link to use the Web UI.

## Key Highlights
* **Parameters**: ~350M (337M DiT acoustic backbone + 13.5M Vocos 24kHz neural vocoder).
* **Sample Rate**: 24,000 Hz studio mono audio.
* **Lexical Stress Support**: Uses explicit `+` markers before stressed vowels (e.g., `прив+ет, к+ак дел+а?`) for natural pronunciation and homograph disambiguation.
* **Zero-Shot Voice Cloning**: High-fidelity timbre cloning using a 3–10 second clean reference audio clip.
* **Format**: Pure `.safetensors` (zero pickle risks, instantaneous tensor loading).

---

## Quickstart (Inference)

### 1. Installation
```bash
pip install f5-tts soundfile torchaudio
```

### 2. Python Code
```python
import torch
import soundfile as sf
from f5_tts.infer.utils_infer import infer_process, load_model, load_vocoder
from f5_tts.model import DiT

device = "cuda" if torch.cuda.is_available() else "cpu"

# Load neural vocoder
vocoder = load_vocoder(vocoder_name="vocos", device=device)

# Load acoustic DiT model
model_cfg = dict(dim=1024, depth=22, heads=16, ff_mult=2, text_dim=512, conv_layers=4)
model = load_model(
    DiT,
    model_cfg,
    "model.safetensors",
    vocab_file="vocab.txt",
    device=device
)

# Zero-shot inference
wave, sr, _ = infer_process(
    ref_audio="reference.wav",
    ref_text="Текст из образца голоса",
    gen_text="Прив+ет! Это русская нейрос+еть для озв+учки.",
    model_obj=model,
    vocoder=vocoder,
    device=device,
    nfe_step=32,
    speed=1.0
)

sf.write("output.wav", wave, sr)
```

---

## Training Details
* **Base Architecture**: F5-TTS DiT Base v2
* **Fine-tuning Dataset**: 14+ hours of studio-grade emotional Russian actor conversations (`langswap/dialogs-ru-emotional-conversations`).
* **Hardware**: Single NVIDIA GeForce RTX 5060 (8GB VRAM).
* **Optimizer**: 8-bit Adam (`bitsandbytes`) with dynamic batching.
* **License**: MIT (Free for commercial and personal use).

# aruntemme/maya2-native-mlx-bf16

[maya-research/maya2-native](https://huggingface.co/maya-research/maya2-native) converted for
[mlx-audio](https://github.com/Blaizzy/mlx-audio) on Apple Silicon: BF16, the reference numerics. All credit for the model goes to
[Maya Research](https://mayaresearch.ai).

Streaming text-to-speech for 11 Indic languages and English, with 20 voices and zero-shot cross-lingual voice cloning.

```bash
pip install -U mlx-audio
mlx_audio.tts.generate --model aruntemme/maya2-native-mlx-bf16 --text "வணக்கம்! நாளைக்கு 2 மணிக்கு meeting இருக்கு." --voice Kayal
```

```python
from mlx_audio.tts.utils import load_model

model = load_model("aruntemme/maya2-native-mlx-bf16")
for result in model.generate("नमस्ते, आपका ऑर्डर कल पहुँच जाएगा।", voice="Ritvik"):
    audio = result.audio  # 24 kHz
```

- **Language:** inferred from the text's script; `lang_code` picks between scripts' languages (hi / mr, bn / as).
- **Cloning:** `ref_audio`, `ref_text` and `ref_lang` clone a 3-10 s clip into any language. Get the speaker's
  permission first.
- **Streaming:** `stream=True`.
- **Text normalisation:** numbers, currency, dates and URLs are spoken correctly in every language
  (`normalize=True`, the default).

See the [mlx-audio docs page](https://github.com/Blaizzy/mlx-audio/blob/main/docs/models/tts/maya2.md) for options,
voices and fidelity checks against the reference implementation.

Converted with `python -m mlx_audio.tts.models.maya2.convert`.

## License and attribution

The weights are Maya Research's, released under the **Apache License 2.0**; see `LICENSE` in this repo.

**Changes from the original:**
- converted from the release's safetensors to the mlx-audio layout (tensor names; tokenizer moved to `tokenizer/`)
- no numeric change (BF16, as released)

**Upstream components keep their own licenses:**
- **Qwen3-1.7B-Base** (Apache-2.0): the backbone the weights were fine-tuned from, included in these weights.
- **Kyutai Mimi** (CC-BY-4.0): the audio codec, downloaded from Kyutai at runtime and not redistributed here.
- **SpeechBrain ECAPA-TDNN** (Apache-2.0): the speaker encoder, downloaded at runtime and not redistributed here.

This conversion is not affiliated with or endorsed by Maya Research.

## Responsible use

This is Maya Research's guidance for the original model, and it applies equally here:
- **Clone only with permission.** Use voices you own or have explicit permission to use.
- **Disclose synthetic speech** to listeners, especially in calls and media.
- **No harmful use.** Never use it for deceptive impersonation, fraud, harassment, non-consensual content,
  disinformation, or to defeat voice authentication.
- **The built-in voices are synthetic personas**, not real people.
- **No watermark.** The model adds no audio watermark, so applications should add their own consent, disclosure and
  abuse safeguards.
